# KatLang constitution — potential semantic-law violations, contradictions, and open questions

> **Q-47, collecting bindings inside clause-family patterns — 2026-11-28 (ONE owner decision, made on 2026-11-27 and recorded and implemented by the task whose brief states it; behavior changed in Lean and C# together; ONE STATUS CHANGE, Q-47 RESOLVED BY DECISION; no registration; totals mechanically recounted; uncommitted over `main` @ `4fab2a56`):** Q-47 (oq FAM-06, registered by the audit of 2026-09-27/28) asked whether the rejection of collecting bindings in clause families was permanent or #99's Stage 2 would land. The owner decided: *A clause family has one fixed call arity. Within any argument, a list or sequence pattern may contain collecting bindings under the ordinary structural-pattern rules.* A collector directly among a family's call arguments stays `InvalidCollectingBinding`, a single literal-free clause keeps its top-level collecting parameter, and the whole same-name group is classified before the family restriction applies. The row moves from § Can wait to § Already resolved with its history. Q-48 and Q-49 stay open. Totals: Q 84 = 57 + 1 + 2 + 24 before and 58 + 1 + 2 + 23 after; PV 54 and X 52 unchanged.

> **Q-57, the position of `xor` on the precedence ladder — 2026-11-28 (ONE owner decision, made on 2026-11-27 and recorded from the brief of the task that records it; no rule text changes in this file; no change in the grammar, Lean or C#; ONE STATUS CHANGE, Q-57 RESOLVED BY DECISION; no registration; totals mechanically recounted; uncommitted over `main` @ `a11ad7fa`):** Q-57 (oq NUM-03, registered by the audit of 2026-09-27/28 and narrowed to the `xor` tier on 2026-11-26) asked for the rationale for placing `xor` between `or` and `and` on the precedence ladder. The owner confirmed the order `or` < `xor` < `and`, from loosest to tightest, and adopted this rationale: *`xor` binds less tightly than `and` so each side of an exclusive choice can express a conjunction. It binds more tightly than `or` so the whole exclusive choice can serve as one alternative in a larger disjunction.* The rationale dates from 2026-11-27; the original reason for the parser's ordering was undocumented. Issue #202 and BOOL-04 govern evaluation separately: `and` and `or` short-circuit, and `xor` needs both Boolean operands. The grammar, the parser's precedence table and the pairwise parse-tree test already state the confirmed order, so no source changes. Q-57's row moves from § Can wait to § Already resolved, where its history, the narrowing of 2026-11-26 included, is kept verbatim. In `constitution.md`, OP-01 states the rationale, and its law-index row and `constitution-summary.md` lose the *Open Q-57* marker and keep *C#-only*. **Totals, recounted mechanically** from the live checkout with the counting scripts of the earlier rounds (`artifacts/validation/q57-xor-precedence/counts/`): before this note, 84 Q IDs = 56 resolved + 1 superseded (Q-43) + 2 partially resolved (Q-35, Q-44) + 25 fully open (27 with an open part; 0 before release), as the Q-51 decision of 2026-11-28 left them; after it, 84 Q IDs = 57 resolved + 1 superseded + 2 partially resolved + 24 fully open (26 with an open part; 0 before release). PV 54 = 25 resolved violations + 21 resolved by decision + 6 intentional exceptions + 2 refuted, and X 52 = 47 resolved + 2 superseded + 3 open, both unchanged.

> **Q-51, a written spread right-hand side of assignment deconstruction — 2026-11-28 (ONE owner decision, recorded from the brief of the task that records it; no rule text changes in this file; no change in Lean or C#; ONE STATUS CHANGE, Q-51 RESOLVED BY DECISION; no registration; totals mechanically recounted; uncommitted over `main` @ `1708b36f`):** Q-51 (oq VAL-05, registered by the audit of 2026-09-27/28) asked whether it is intended that a spread right-hand side opens one level further than the bare value: `x, y = [(1, 2)]*` succeeds, while `x, y = [(1, 2)]` is `ArityMismatch`. The owner decided that it is. *Assignment deconstruction captures the right-hand side's output rows into one value using ordinary capture. A written spread contributes its immediate items to that capture. If it contributes the only item, capture returns that item itself. Deconstruction then opens the captured value one level under VAR-05 and binds the targets. A list or sequence exposed by singleton capture can therefore supply its immediate elements to the targets.* The binding follows from the value supplied, and naming the intermediate value explains exactly what the inline spelling does. Lean and C# already implement the decision, and existing tests, Lean guards and conformance cases pin it, so neither engine changes. Q-51's row moves from § Can wait to § Already resolved, where its history is kept verbatim. In `constitution.md`, VAR-05, its law-index row and `constitution-summary.md` lose the *Open Q-51* marker and keep *Open Q-84*, the independent question about argument views. **Totals, recounted mechanically** with the counting scripts of the earlier rounds (`artifacts/validation/q51-deconstruction-spread/counts/`): before this note, 84 Q IDs = 55 resolved + 1 superseded (Q-43) + 2 partially resolved (Q-35, Q-44) + 26 fully open (28 with an open part; 0 before release), as in the inventory of 2026-11-15 and the recount of 2026-11-26; after it, 84 Q IDs = 56 resolved + 1 superseded + 2 partially resolved + 25 fully open (27 with an open part; 0 before release). PV 54 = 25 resolved violations + 21 resolved by decision + 6 intentional exceptions + 2 refuted, and X 52 = 47 resolved + 2 superseded + 3 open, both unchanged.

Its question, "record the rationale for non-short-circuit `and`/`or` and for the `xor` tier", rested in its first half on a rule that the owner decision of issue #202 (`65b1b136`, 2026-11-23) replaced: `and` and `or` now short-circuit, and `xor` stays eager because its result needs both operands. That half leaves no question, so Q-57 keeps only its `xor`-tier part (OP-01): no issue or decision records why `xor` sits between `or` and `and`. Q-57 stays OPEN in § Can wait, and BOOL-04 no longer carries its marker. The result boundary decided by Q-25 remains resolved. > **Line-final star attachment — Q-65 owner refinement, issue #183, 2026-10-14 (owner decision; no Q, PV or X status change; totals unchanged; uncommitted over `main` @ `2cc6b56b`):** the owner approved katlangorg/katlangnet#183: when `*` follows a completed expression and is the final significant token of its physical line (EOF included; comments and blank lines change nothing), an ATTACHED `expr*` is the postfix spread marker and completes the expression, while a DETACHED `expr *` is multiplication and leaves it incomplete. The canonical newline rule — "Newlines separate complete expressions by default. An incomplete expression continues when valid syntax permits it, without consuming a new declaration. Otherwise, an independent expression or declaration begins a new construct. Syntax that cannot stand alone but can legally continue the preceding expression attaches backward. All decisions are syntactic, never based on evaluated values." — remains the authority; the star rule is a narrower syntactic classification feeding it. This supersedes the Q-65 subrule of the same day that every physical line-final star announces multiplication (EOF included), and narrows SYN-12's "attachment never influences classification" and A22's whitespace invariant to stars with a same-line follower; it adopts, as a refinement of resolved Q-65 rather than a new question, the attached/detached newline rule that #140 introduced, #161 reversed and Q-33 rejected as P4A. C#-only surface syntax: no Lean production rule, theorem or guard changes; spread/capture VALUE semantics, repeated spread, demand and arithmetic are unchanged. SYN-11 (title, status, rule, bullets, examples, evidence), SYN-08, SYN-12, VAL-07, VAL-08, SUP-01, SUP-05, OP-01, OP-02, A21, A22 and the Q-65 current-rule restatements carry dated notes; superseded text is retained. Evidence: `artifacts/validation/line-final-star-attachment/`.

> **Q-81 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-12 (historical inventory; superseded by the R8/X-13 note above; committed as `c22662ec`; owner decision, variadic postfix selection; Lean and C# changed together; original resolution over `main` @ `3e244f91`):** the owner approved the GitHub issue replacing `:` indexing with variadic postfix `[]` selection — **RESOLVED BY OWNER DECISION**: *(A) PARENTHESES INVOKE A COMPUTATION; POSTFIX BRACKETS SELECT FROM A VALUE; selection never changes how its receiver obtains that value (`Data` cached, `Data()` fresh). (B) `count`, `first`, `last` and selection share ONE immediate positional view: a list or sequence offers its immediate elements, any other value — a string included — is itself at position 0, and `()` and `[]` have none. (C) Over a value in hand, `first(v) ≡ v[0]` and `last(v) ≡ v[count(v) - 1]`, errors included — laws, never rewrites of effectful expressions. (D) One element per supplied index, kept whole; only the result grouping is normalized: zero selections `()`, one the element, several one sequence. (E) The receiver is demanded once; the selector supply is formed like a call's (explicit spreads during formation, ordinary selectors suspended); the supplied indices are demanded, validated and selected left to right up to the first failure. (F) A `[` on the receiver's physical line (spaces and tabs allowed) opens the selector list, which may then span lines; a later-line `[` begins a list literal; commas select siblings and chained brackets descend; `A*[0]` stays multiplication; a selection has no callable identity; `:` is retired with a migration diagnostic.* Q-81 is registered for this decision and is resolved by it, and it resolves **Q-52** (the selector grammar). Inventory: **81 IDs** — **48 resolved** (Q-52 and Q-81 this round), **1 superseded**, **1 partially resolved** (Q-44), **31 needing a decision**; 32 IDs have an open part, none in § Decide before release. PV and X unchanged. No rule is added or retired; the amended rules are listed in § Already resolved, Q-81.

> **Q-37 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-11 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-80 resolution above; committed as `516a381c`; original resolution over `main` @ `43292ed7`; owner decision; Lean and C# changed together):** the owner decided Q-37 — the re-entrant read of a zero-parameter property (EFF-07; CB-09) — **RESOLVED BY OWNER DECISION — the outermost successful evaluation owns the entry**: *the OUTERMOST successful property-style evaluation of a cache key owns its entry.* (1) A property-style read that misses while no evaluation of the same key is running owns the key. (2) A read of the same key while its owner is still running — directly or through other properties and calls, an explicit call's frame included — is re-entrant: it evaluates and returns its own, possibly intermediate, result, but publishes nothing. (3) Only the owner's success is published; every later ordinary read reuses it; publication never replaces an entry. (4) A failed owner publishes nothing for its key; entries other keys' owners published stay. (5) An explicit `A()` owns nothing. The owner chose neither option the § Can wait row recorded (return the stored first entry, or document the difference): `A = if(tick() < 3, A + 1, 0)` / `A, A` was `S[2, 0]` and is now `S[2, 2]` after the same three ticks; the seeded reproduction (`Classify(r) = if(r == 796, 1, if(r == 339, 2, 3))` / `tick = Classify(randomInt(0, 1000))` / `A = if(tick() < 3, A + 1, 0)` / `A, A`, seed 7) prints `2`, `2` after exactly three draws (796, 339, 489; formerly `2`, `0`). *Implementation:* C# `ZeroArgPropertyPublications` (both run-scoped caches, both members of the async one), Lean `EvalState.activeZeroArgProperties` with `evalZeroArgPropertyAccessCounted`; `OutermostPropertyCachePublicationTests` and `CoreTests/PropertyCachePublication.lean` pin it. > **Q-45 resolution, 2026-10-10 (historical inventory; superseded by the X-18 closeout above; committed as `a024eeaf`; original resolution over `main` @ `5041bffe`; no C# or Lean behavior change):** the owner decided Q-45 — the evaluation order of `.string(args)` (oq DOT-03; PV-38) — **RESOLVED BY OWNER DECISION — the current Model-C behavior is kept as intended**: *the `.string` intrinsic accepts exactly zero supplied arguments, and a written argument list follows the ordinary Model-C call steps.* (1) The written argument supply is formed; (2) explicit arbitrary spreads execute during that formation; (3) ordinary non-spread computations stay suspended; (4) a nonzero supplied argument count is rejected with `ArityMismatch` before the receiver or any ordinary argument is demanded; (5) a supply of zero items reaches the intrinsic, which then demands the receiver's VALUE and converts it to its numeric text; (6) extension fallback calls follow their own ordinary demand semantics (DOT-03). There is no universal receiver-first rule and no argument-first rule for `.string`. The question was posed against the pre-Model-C order; Model C (2026-10-02) superseded its premise, and the owner accepted the order the Phase A2 re-run (2026-10-09) recorded. *Verification:* the production seams (C# `RejectDotStringIntrinsicArguments` with its async twin, Lean `rejectDotStringIntrinsicArguments`) and the existing six-route pins establish the law unchanged; two six-route rows (`trace(5).string`, `trace(5).string()`) and five Lean guards (`CoreTests/Strings.lean` § Q-45, trace-free twins of the order) were added. > **Q-33 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-09 (historical inventory; superseded by the FA-OQ-1 resolution above; committed as `d7dae7d8`; original implementation over `main` @ `4d7cac19`):** the owner decided Q-33 — P0: the current parse is law; no new diagnostic — the recommendation of `../q33-parser-boundary-investigation/final-report.md`. *The law (SYN-11):* a line-final star is no exception: a `*` at the end of a physical line is classified by SYN-11 exactly like any other `*`; if the next significant token, including across blank lines or comments, can begin an operand and does not begin a declaration, the star is binary multiplication, and expression parsing then continues across the newline under SYN-08 with ordinary precedence unchanged (`X = A*` newline `X` is `X = A * X`, which leaves no output row; `x, y = V*` newline `x + y` is `(V * x) + y`, never `V * (x + y)`); the layout alone introduces no warning or error. A spread row that another row follows ends with `A*,`; a definition body ending in a spread is closed as `X = (A*)` or `X = { A* }`; a following declaration head also ends the expression. Rejected: a warning (P1, P1ANY), a new error (P2A, P2B), and newline rules that would silently change accepted values (P4A, P4B). *(Issue #183, 2026-10-14: the attached/detached line-final newline rule that P4A prototyped was later adopted by owner decision as a refinement of Q-65 — see "Line-final star attachment" above)* *Implementation:* no production parser, evaluator, diagnostic, grammar, AST, Lean-semantics or public-API change — documentation (AGENTS.md, `syntax.md`, `KatLang.ebnf`, `tutorial.md`, `SEMANTIC-ALIGNMENT.md`), the new `LineFinalStarLawTests`, the repaired `ModuleCoordinateSpaceTests` spread fixture, and the regenerated spec case `line-final-star-in-definition-continues`. **Q-33 RESOLVED BY DECISION; § Decide before release now holds no open question** (the other open questions stay open). > **X-49 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-08 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-33 resolution above; committed as `4d7cac1`):** the owner decided X-49 — FRONT-FIRST MOVEMENT, POSTFIX FIRST, the law selected after `../x49-grace-ordering-investigation/movement-followup/final-report.md` (the earlier Target Order proposal is not adopted). *The law (PAR-06 Movement, Order of movement, Residual weights):* an owner's OWN inferred names start in first semantic occurrence with their exact summed weights (unbounded integers); every name with a POSITIVE weight takes one turn, from the LAST-occurring to the first-occurring, then every name with a NEGATIVE weight, from the FIRST-occurring to the last-occurring; a turn exchanges the name with its neighbour one unit at a time until its remaining weight is zero, it reaches the end of the own list, or the neighbour moves the same way with at least as much REMAINING weight (the patent's strict comparison of current remaining weights); a passed name keeps its weight; unused weight stays and keeps blocking; nothing crosses the own/lifted boundary. `K = s * 100 + ~x * 10 + ~y` is `K(x, y, s)`, `Z = s~ * 100 + x~ * 10 + y` is `Z(y, s, x)`, `K = a * 100 + b~ * 10 + ~~c` is `K(c, a, b)` (formerly `K(a, c, b)`: the 2021 position cursor skipped the displaced `c`), `K = a~ * 100 + b * 10 + ~c` is `K(b, c, a)` (prefix-first would give `(c, a, b)`), and `F = ~a * 100 + b * 10 + ~~c` is `F(a, c, b)`. *Implementation (C#-only by design):* the internal `GraceMovement` replaces `ParameterDetector`'s position cursor; weights are exact (`System.Numerics.BigInteger`; the int-saturating memo effect is deleted, the shared-node memo keeps exact per-visit deltas); no eligibility (Q-16 G-O), grammar, lifting, evaluator, Lean-semantics, diagnostic or public-API change; a standalone Lean model is `lean/CoreTests/GraceMovement.lean`. **X-49 RESOLVED BY DECISION.** Rules reconciled: PAR-06 (title, status, law, rule, examples, caveat, tension, evidence), PAR-03/PAR-05 and DOT-06 (evidence pointers), the PAR topic tail. 79 Q IDs: 40 resolved, 1 superseded, 1 partial, 37 fully open (38 with an open part; > **Q-16 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-07 (historical inventory; superseded by the X-49 resolution above; committed as `f314cf6`):** the owner decided Q-16 — G-O, owner-local Grace: Q-16(1) E (eligibility, not movement) and Q-16(2) O (nested inferred owners retain their own Grace), the recommendation of `../q16-grace-investigation/final-report.md` (worktree `q16-grace-ownership-81ee86`). *The law (PAR-06):* Grace belongs to the owner whose written rows contain the marked occurrence — the root, a property body, a brace block in any position, a clause-branch body; output rows and deconstruction right-hand sides (`WrittenRows`), so hoisting never moves an occurrence to another owner. A marker is valid exactly when that occurrence becomes one of the owner's OWN inferred parameters; its weight is applied as far as the ordering allows, and saturation is never an error (`F = ~x + 1`, an already-first `~x`, an already-last `x~`, excess weight, a tie, a cancelled weight, and `A = p - q` / `F = A - z~` — `F(z, p, q)` — are valid). A fixed binding (explicit parameter or clause binder, enclosing parameter, property, builtin, opened name, structural member, `.string`) and every occurrence on a closed level (a written list; a clause branch's own rows) stay `InvalidGraceMarker`. *Branch nesting (PAT-04):* a branch is closed at its own level only; an algorithm nested in it is an ordinary owner in every spelling (`Apply(f) = f(1, 10)` / `F(0) = Apply({ y - ~x })` / `F(0)` is `9`, like the named `B = y - ~x`), its parameters never added to the branch, and a branch binder it captures is an enclosing parameter (`F(n) = Apply({ x - ~n })` is `InvalidGraceMarker`, one report). *Implementation (C#-only by design):* the parser's lexical branch-body Grace scan (`FindGraceSpan` / `ScanPendingForGraceSpan`) is deleted; the parameter detector's per-owner rewrite pass is the one authority (`GraceEffectPolicy.ClosedBranch` replaces `NotReported`); eligibility wording ("Grace cannot reorder 'x' because …"); `ApplyGraceReordering` unchanged; a load-bearing branch's own-level verdict comes when that deferred unit is selected (MOD-10). No evaluator, Lean-semantics, grammar or public-API change; Lean docstrings narrowed. **Q-16 RESOLVED BY DECISION; X-08 and X-39 RESOLVED; PV-28 RESOLVED BY DECISION;** oq LIFT-10 is closed; candidate **X-49** (PAR-06's ordering prose does not fully determine `ApplyGraceReordering`'s multi-marker order: `K = a * 100 + b~ * 10 + ~~c` is `K(a, c, b)`, without `b~` `K(c, a, b)`) is recorded open, not decided. > **Q-28 + Q-10 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-07 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-16 resolution above; committed as `66367a6`):** the owner decided Q-28 (N-F) and Q-10 (D-F); the decisions are independent. *Value, representation, presentation (Q-28 N-F; new VAL-11):* `==` — `Decimal128.Equals` at numeric leaves, recursively structural — is the language's one “same value” relation for `==`/`!=`, `contains`, `distinct`, numeric literal patterns, duplicate clause heads and repeated-name compatibility; a number's Decimal128 representation (quantum, zero sign, NaN sign) is data the value carries, never provenance, preserved by value-carrying operations and observable through `.string`; a repeated name keeps ONE richest compatible complete contribution (NEED-04) and, among equally rich ones, the FIRST in written traversal order, its representation included (`P(x, x) = x.string`: `P(1.5, 1.50)` is `'1.5'`, `P(1.50, 1.5)` is `'1.50'`; with `A = 1.50`, `P(1.5, A)` and `P(A, 1.5)` are `'1.50'`); Permuting all contributions of one repeated name preserves satisfiability. On success it preserves the bound VALUE up to `==`, callable identity and channel availability; among equally rich compatible contributions, the first in written traversal order supplies the retained representation. Failure reporting follows ordinary binding order (NEED-04, PAT-10, Q-27): when different incompatibilities coexist, permutation may change the error category, blamed contribution, payload, message or span, although every permutation still fails. Collections keep their own representative rules; COLL-06's `orderDesc` question and OP-13's same-signed quantum tie are not decided. No production change: N-F is the existing C# (`BindNeedPatterns`) and Lean (`bindNeedName`) behavior. *Composable display filters (Q-10 D-F):* every active `DisplayDecimals` setting is a presentation filter — the program root's own property (source) and `RunOptions.DefaultDisplayDecimals` / CLI `--display-decimals` (host) compose by their minimum; an absent filter imposes no limit, neither present is canonical display, and host `null` is no filter. The source filter stays an engine-level convention: `KatLangEngine` reads it after successful output with the ordinary cached value read in the same run, whatever the host filter is (it can trace, draw, spend steps, be cancelled or fail); raw `Evaluator.Run*` never reads it, an intentional boundary. The investigation recommended D-O (no source hook); the owner rejected D-O after the product-portability discussion and adopted D-F; the only production change is `KatLangEngine.CombineDisplayDecimals`. **Q-28 and Q-10 RESOLVED BY DECISION; X-28 and X-12 RESOLVED; X-35 RESOLVED BY DECISION (intentional engine/evaluator boundary);** oq NUM-01, FAM-09 and RUN-03 are closed. > **Q-19 + Q-29 + Q-31 + Q-32 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-06 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-28 + Q-10 resolution above; committed as `83819f3`):** the owner decided Q-19 (D-I), Q-29 (A-U), Q-31 (H-P) and Q-32 (I-U) of `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md` together as one law system for `open` and loaded modules. *Open providers (Q-19 D-I):* an `open` list counts the PROVIDERS its targets resolve to by the one callable identity — the declaration in its declaring scope, NEED-04's relation — never by spelling or position: `open Sub, Lib.Sub` for one declaration is one provider, `open M, M` and `open M, (M)` stay one, two written blocks or two declarations stay two however equal. *Static ambiguity (Q-29 A-U):* provider overlap is legal; a WRITTEN name whose lookup reaches an open level with two or more different providers is the front-end error `AmbiguousOpen` at the occurrence, whether or not evaluation demands it; a dot fallback name counts only when the edge certainly takes it (Q-75 MUST); a receiver-decided fallback and a host-built tree keep the run-time `AmbiguousOpen`. *Module hygiene (Q-31 H-P):* a loaded module is a source unit rooted at the prelude whatever holds it — its free names resolve in its own declarations and the prelude, never at the load site; a name it cannot resolve is its member's implicit parameter, and a site parameter reaches a member only by an explicit argument, bare forwarding or formula lifting — so `open 'u'` ≡ `M = load('u')` + `open M` ≡ `M.Member`. *Module identity (Q-32 I-U):* one canonical URL is ONE module declaration per compiled program — one elaborated module, one member binding, one callable identity, one open provider; holders stay bindings of their own for the module's output; distinct canonical URLs stay distinct. **Q-19, Q-29, Q-31 and Q-32 RESOLVED BY DECISION; X-20, X-26 and X-37 RESOLVED; PV-41 and PV-42 RESOLVED BY DECISION;** oq NAME-01, NAME-02, MOD-01 and MOD-02 are closed. > **Q-17 + Q-18 + Q-75 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-05 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-19 + Q-29 + Q-31 + Q-32 resolution above; committed as `8ead770`):** the owner decided Q-17 (S-C), Q-18 (C-B3) and Q-75 (F-A) of `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md` together as one identity-oriented dot semantics. *The route:* an ordinary non-spread edge `R.n(args?)` selects a DECLARED structural member `n` whatever its spelling — `string` included — with accessibility checked after selection; a member declared only in clause branches is `LocalOnlyProperty`; on a structural miss `n == string` is the number-to-text intrinsic, otherwise the edge is the extension fallback `n(R, args)`; a lexical `string` is never consulted by `.string`, and `R*.n(args)` stays `n(R*, args)`. *The identity:* a dot expression has ONE callable identity in every algorithm-capable position — supplied argument, forwarded parameter, builtin callback, loop step and callee: an argumentless structural path carries its member's own callable (aliases normalized), and every other dot expression is a calculation value; parentheses never change identity, so `(Box.G)(2)` is `Box.G(2)` and `(Box.V)()` is the fresh call `Box.V()`, and a call may follow only a name, a graced name, an argumentless dot edge or a redundant group of one (`X.Mk(1)()` is `UnseparatedSameLineItem`, like `Mk(1)()`). *The static obligation:* the existing `LexicalFallbackSelection` lattice decides — an inferring body collects a fallback name unless the selection is `Never`; a closed explicit list or clause-branch body checks it only when the selection is `Always` (`Get(obj) = 5.size` is the same `UndeclaredIdentifier` as `Get(obj) = size(5)`, at the member token, worded receiver-aware); a MAY-selected fallback stays a run-time question. **Q-17, Q-18 and Q-75 RESOLVED BY DECISION; X-21 RESOLVED; X-20 narrowed (its open-dedup row stays open for Q-19); PV-09, PV-15 and PV-22 RESOLVED BY DECISION;** oq DOT-01 and DOT-02 are closed. The paired Lean/C# implementation decides the route from one property lookup in both languages, routes the callee through the one CALLABLE projection (Lean `resolveCalleeAlg` over `projectNeedStructuralMember`; C# `ProjectDotPathCallable`, also read by the sequence optimizer), narrows the parser's call gate, retires the C#-only qualified-Math resolution, and checks a certain fallback name in the C# front end (Lean models no front-end rule, FORMAL-02). > **Q-06 + Q-27 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-05 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-17 + Q-18 + Q-75 resolution above; committed as `ad3d7dd`):** the owner decided Q-06 (option (a)) and Q-27 (policy P2 of `../q27-q06-error-policy/final-report.md`) together as one evaluation-error taxonomy: *an evaluation error names the first semantic contract the executed operation cannot satisfy, in that operation's ordinary evaluation order.* Missing CALLABLE capability in any invoking position — a user higher-order parameter, a builtin callback, a `repeat`/`while` step, an invoking slot reached through a builtin used as a step — is `NotAnAlgorithm`, decided by CALLABLE projection only when execution needs to invoke the slot (never by demanding VALUE; an unused slot is never projected); a present VALUE of the wrong kind is `TypeMismatch` (`-()`, `sum((1, true))`, `A:[0]`, `range([1], 3)`, `take(xs, 'x')`); supply/output cardinality is `ArityMismatch`; a selection naming no position is `BadIndex`, `first`/`last` on an empty collection included, so `first(A) ≡ A:0` and `last(A) ≡ A:(count(A) - 1)` hold for every target, errors included; a zero divisor is `DivisionByZero` and every other valid-kind domain failure `IllegalInEval` (`min(())`, `take(xs, 1.5)`). A callable keeps its ordinary binder verdicts (`A = 7` / `map([1, 2], A)` is `ArityMismatch`), and NEED-04's repeated-name categories are unchanged. No public error-code member is added, removed or renumbered, and no successful program changes value, count, demand or effects. **Q-06 and Q-27 RESOLVED BY DECISION; X-11, X-30 and X-31 RESOLVED; PV-30 and PV-34 RESOLVED BY DECISION;** oq EFF-03 and ERR-01 are closed. The paired Lean/C# implementation changes the same functions in both languages (one invoking-slot projection, `projectInvokingSlot` / `ProjectInvokingSlot`; `expectInt`; unary minus; the collection-element check; the whole-number control; the empty policy as metadata, `requireSelectablePosition`); wording-only messages name the repeated-name and `while`-flag contracts, and builtin arity payloads carry their real minimum. Rules reconciled: FORMAL-06 (the taxonomy is constitutional), FORMAL-08, OP-04, OP-14, VAL-04, VAL-08, VAL-10, BOOL-03, CMP-05, SEQ-04 (the total selection law), SEQ-05, COLL-05 (the split empty policy), COLL-08, COLL-09, COLL-10, LOOP-05, LOOP-08, HO-01, HO-04, HO-05, SUP-07, CALL-03 and NEED-06 (a dated clarification, no new NEED law); wording-only quotes in PAT-09, PAT-10, LOOP-02, LOOP-03 and LOOP-06. 79 Q IDs: 30 resolved, 1 superseded, 2 partial, 46 fully open (48 with an open part; 11 before release). > **Q-23 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-04 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-06 + Q-27 resolution above; committed as `927a8c4`):** the owner decided Q-23 (option Q23-B of `../q23-investigation/final-report.md`): *a loop step is an ordinary callable invoked over the current state supply* — any callable is eligible as a `while`/`repeat` step, and when an iteration executes, the current state slots are supplied to it through KatLang's ordinary invocation semantics; loops specialize only the iteration protocol and the row receiver. The paired Lean/C# implementation invokes each step through its own ordinary machinery — a user algorithm through its binder, a clause family through the ordinary family dispatcher (clause order, inspecting patterns, non-match versus failure), a builtin through its argument roles, an alias as its target — and reads a builtin's ONE result value as ONE next-state row (`()` included). Eligibility never depends on category, representation, clause count, spelling or planner support; a value with no callable identity is still no step (NEED-06), and a zero-iteration `repeat` never projects its step. **Q-23 RESOLVED BY DECISION; PV-12 RESOLVED;** X-23's message now describes only values and zero-parameter steps. Over the investigation's 1,796 probe variants no accepted program changed (461 formerly rejected programs now succeed, 189 fail with the callee's own ordinary failure, 19 are still rejected). Rules reconciled: LOOP-08 (replaced), LOOP-02 (title; binding generalized), LOOP-03 (a builtin's one row), LOOP-05 (never projected), LOOP-01 (Model-C cleanup: initial slots are supplied, not demanded), PAT-11 (a family is a step), HO-02 (caveat), RES-06, COLL-01 and SYN-05 (evidence, tension or the PV-12 reference). 79 Q IDs: 28 resolved, 1 superseded, 2 partial, 48 fully open (50 with an open part; 13 before release). > **Q-24 + Q-26 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-04 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-23 resolution above; committed as `f6d978c`):** the owner decided Q-24 and Q-26 together as one loop cardinality law — *patterns bind, rows produce, `*` opens; none of the three changes the others* — and the paired Lean/C# implementation resolves PV-46, X-24 and X-33. **Q-24 RESOLVED BY DECISION — LOOP-04 packing removed:** a step's parameter patterns inspect and bind the incoming state only and never change how its output becomes the next state; an explicit spread in a step row has its ordinary meaning (it opens one value boundary and supplies the items), so `Dup(x, x) = { (x + 1, x + 1)* }` forms the same next state as `Dup(x, x) = { x + 1, x + 1 }`; repeated names, structural patterns and collectors constrain the next binding but never repack the outgoing state; LOOP-04 is retired into LOOP-03, and the pattern-derived packing flag and its machinery are deleted in Lean and C#. **Q-26 RESOLVED BY DECISION — loop results are ordinary value boundaries:** `while`/`repeat` return ONE value, the canonical capture of the final state's slots (`()`, the slot itself, or a sequence), with emitted count `Result.valueCount` like every other builtin and call result; a non-spread loop expression is one item at every receiver (root, body, capture, list, loop step, callback body) and only `L*` opens it — so `Fibonacci.repeat(10, 0, 1)` is one row `(55, 89)`, VAL-06/07/08/09 lose their loop exceptions and SUP-01 loses its "sole exception". The step's rows remain the loop's own next-state protocol, and `while` still reads its flag from their last item. **Q-23 stays OPEN**, narrowed to which callables may receive the incoming state and how they are dispatched; no callable category gained or lost acceptance. Rules reconciled: LOOP-02, LOOP-03 (LOOP-04 merged), LOOP-07, LOOP-08 (evidence), SUP-01, SUP-02, VAL-06, VAL-07, VAL-08, VAL-09, HO-03 (caveat), NEED-04 (clarification, no new law). 79 Q IDs: 27 resolved, 1 superseded, 2 partial, 49 fully open (51 with an open part; 14 before release). > **Q-09 resolution and implementation, 2026-10-04 (historical inventory; superseded by the Q-24 + Q-26 resolution above; committed as `3fbaad9`):** the owner decided Q-09 by splitting it, and the implementation fixes PV-07 and closes X-34. **Q-09a ACCEPTED — host-stack headroom is host policy:** whether the host-stack backstop stops a run may depend on the execution route, genuine suspension, the host thread and its stack size, the build, the runtime and its JIT state, and the platform; KatLang promises the language-visible failure kind `EvaluationStackExhausted`, never a recursion depth or equal physical-stack capacity across routes or environments. **Q-09b ACCEPTED — limits observe a run; they never choose how it runs:** configuring, raising or removing a limit that the run does not reach changes nothing about that run — not its value, effects, budget accounting, or whether it completes; the limit-selected execution strategy is rejected. **PV-07 RESOLVED:** `Evaluator.CreateRootCtx` no longer disables loop planning or sequence fusion because `MaxSteps`, `MaxMaterializedItems`, `MaxStringLength` or `MaxMaterializedStringChars` is configured; every strategy instead charges every budget identically (a planned loop charges the generic per-iteration step and exactly the generic expression-work checkpoints; the fused filter→count pipeline records the elided stage heads and reserves, without allocating, the generic composition's items), so steps, raw checkpoints, peak depth, materialized items and string units are equal on every strategy, exactly. The witness `R(n) = if(n > 0, range(n, n).filter({ R(x - 1) >= 0 }).count, 0)` / `R(35)` (Release, 1.5 MiB thread) is `ok 1` under all 17 probed configurations, formerly `EvaluationStackExhausted` under any of the four former selectors. **X-34 RESOLVED:** the public documentation states both directions of the twin's headroom and no longer calibrates `MaxSupportedDepth` against the host stack (mechanically pinned). RUN-01 (exceptions 1 and 2, boundary, known tension), RUN-02 (its determinism clause) and RUN-03 (strategy-neutral semantic limits; the host stack as an environmental backstop) are reconciled; no other rule text changes, and Lean is unchanged (it models no limits, strategies, host stack, async or JIT). 79 Q IDs: 25 resolved, 1 superseded, 2 partial, 51 fully open (53 with an open part; 16 before release). Five findings have been fixed since, all on 2026-09-28: PV-02 (GitHub issue [#171](https://github.com/katlangorg/katlangnet/issues/171)), in the working tree over `a2700f4` (later committed as `3e57a08`); PV-04, after the owner decided open question Q-01 (at-most-once argument value evaluation), in the working tree over `3e57a08` (later committed as `33c9971`); PV-06, after the owner decided open question Q-02 (every encountered resource-limit failure is terminal for the run), committed as `c6813ef` on branch `claude/lucid-mccarthy-9yy1s2` (the same tree is `a4ae04a` on `main`); and PV-03 with PV-27, after the owner decided open question Q-03 (a callable that works with no arguments is read by its bare name, so implicit lifting skips it), in the working tree over `df3f8b0` (later committed as `13196f8`). The owner then decided open question Q-04 (automatic parameter forwarding must not change what an existing name refers to; it reuses parameter bindings only), implemented in the working tree over `13196f8` (not yet committed); that decision resolves PV-01 — which the audit had refuted as a violation and left a disputed design question — by changing the behavior PV-01 described. The owner then decided open question Q-05 (a repeated parameter name is a compatibility constraint over independently supplied arguments; matching may restrict a binding but never manufacture one), implemented in the working tree over `abe1383` (not yet committed); that decision resolves PV-13 — an intentional exception whose covering rule it reversed — and X-17. Their records are kept, with the resolutions, under § Resolved violations; Q-01, Q-02, Q-03, Q-04 and Q-05 moved to § Already resolved. The Q-05 hostile review also raised the post-audit open question Q-72 (implicit lifting collapsed a callee's repeated parameter name into one forwarded parameter); the owner decided it the same day with its option (c) — a callable whose parameter patterns repeat a binding name does not take part in implicit forwarding, and the program writes the call — implemented in the working tree over `abe1383` together with Q-05 and committed with it as `515ed3c`; Q-72 moved to § Already resolved. The owner reversed the Q-72 decision the same day in favor of the general rule *implicit forwarding is by binding name, regardless of how many times that name occurs in a callee's parameter patterns*, committed as `c719f43`; Q-72 stays under § Already resolved, with the reversal recorded. PV-05, PV-19 and PV-20 were then fixed together on 2026-09-29 without a new decision — the rules already required the behavior (CALL-03: callback slots are never demanded during assembly; HO-04: `reduce`'s `initial` is a value slot; SUP-01, SUP-02 and CALL-04: a spread supplies its items, or its failure is the call's, before arity) — as one repair of the collection-builtin argument adapter in Lean and C# (builtin call assembly respects argument roles), in the working tree over `c719f43` (later committed as `641d81d`); their records moved to § Resolved violations, Q-06 keeps only its part (1), and X-30 is narrowed to it. PV-11, PV-24, PV-25 and PV-49 were then fixed on 2026-09-29, again without a new decision — MOD-01, MOD-02 and MOD-03, MOD-05, and PAR-06 and PAT-04 already required the behavior — in the working tree over `641d81d` (later committed as `bb0e543`): every open target is validated statically through one head-and-steps decomposition (C# front end; PV-11), the `open` placement check counts clause definitions (parser; PV-25), the branch Grace scan covers every row a branch writes (parser; PV-49), and Lean's `elaborateClauseGroup` gives a clause family no opens of its own (Lean; PV-24); their records moved to § Resolved violations, and X-05, X-06 and X-10 are resolved with them. PV-08 was then fixed on 2026-09-29, again without a new decision and without a new rule — FWD-02 and PAR-07 already required an alias to mean the explicit call it abbreviates, and FWD-02 is amended to state the exact item-supply reconstruction that forbids PV-08 directly — in the working tree over `bb0e543` (not yet committed): implicit forwarding rebuilds a callee's sequence-value group from exactly the items its captures stand for (C# front end); its record moved to § Resolved violations. The same day the owner decided the structural-pattern model, which superseded that repair (Q-20 resolved, Q-73 raised), and then the alias and wrapper rules — `A = F` aliases F exactly, `A(params) = F` calls F with A's own parameter supply, and `A = F(exprs)` infers only the names written in `exprs` — both in the working tree over `bb0e543` (not yet committed): PV-08's record gains its fourth stage, Q-73 is resolved, and the new Q-74 records the composite exception (formula lifting still reads callee binder names). On 2026-09-30 the owner finalized FWD-02 — `A(p) = F` is bare forwarding by compatible existing binding NAME, never the positional call `A(p) = F(p)` — in the same working tree: Q-74 is resolved as that deliberate distinction, and PV-08 gains its final stage. The Q-02 synchronization also narrowed PV-07 (still active) and added the post-audit entries PV-50 and Q-71. The Q-03 synchronization closed X-15 and added dated notes to the still-open entries whose collecting-only witnesses it changed (PV-21, PV-31, X-02, X-38, Q-14, Q-15); the other statuses are unchanged. The original PV-01 through PV-49 entries were found by 14 hostile hunters and each was verified by two independent adversarial verifiers (a reproduce/refute lens and a mechanism/intent/Lean lens). Where the lenses disagreed, the more conservative verdict is reported and the disagreement stated. The top findings were re-run independently afterwards (see that table). On 2026-09-30 the owner then decided, in the working tree over `4bea2e4` (not yet committed), first X-02 — inferred signatures are held to the rules of written ones, so a formula that would compose two collectors at one pattern level is the definition's front-end `InvalidCollectingBinding`, never a host exception — and then the unified formula-lifting law: a formula lifts a reference exactly when its immediate consumer uses it as a VALUE and the callable it resolves to, whatever its category or route, has a lifting signature that requires supplied arguments (clause families named by their clauses, `UnliftableClauseFamily` otherwise). That resolves Q-11 with PV-21, and the FORMULA halves of Q-12 (PV-26) and Q-13 (PV-14); their alias halves stay open with FWD-02, whose eligibility is unchanged. Q-15 is unchanged except that its diagnostic is not observed beneath a lazy `if` branch. Re-verified unchanged by the same re-run (`artifacts/validation/formula-lifting-law/rerun/`): PV-03 and Q-03 (a callable that accepts zero supplied arguments is never lifted), Q-04 (forwarding reuses existing parameter bindings only; the five Q-04 corpus programs that changed are new lifting positions and categories, each reusing exactly the binding the source rule selects), PV-08 and Q-73 (structural kinds are rebuilt as themselves), and Q-74 (formula lifting, bare forwarding and explicit calls stay three distinct mechanisms).

## Potential semantic-law violations

This section records every candidate in which one execution path, spelling or context appears to take a different route from its equivalent and thereby break a stated law. It is the class of defect that issue #170 (fixed in ebf623e) belonged to.

**Sources.** The original PV-01 through PV-49 candidates came from hunters and were checked independently through two lenses. PV-50 was a post-audit hypothesis, later reproduced before Model C and now resolved with its dated evidence preserved below:
- the **repro** lens: does it reproduce, and is it really forbidden by the rules as written?
- the **intent** lens: is the behaviour a principled, documented exception, or an accidental route?

**Status rule.** When the two lenses agree, their verdict is the status. When they disagree, the weaker claim is the status, and the disagreement is stated. The order from weakest to strongest is: refuted < intentional exception < suspicious but unconfirmed < likely violation < confirmed violation. Severity is given per lens when the lenses differ.

**Probes.** Probe files live under `scratchpad/probes/<dir>/` and run with `scratchpad/probe/bin/KatLang.ParserFuzz.exe FILE [flags] -q`, which compares five paths: engine, engineAsync, generic, optimized and twin. Every C# output quoted in the violation entries was re-run for this section against HEAD a2700f4 (the probe runner is built from it). Lean outputs and `dotnet fsi` harness outputs are quoted from the verifiers' runs and are labelled as such. "(all 5 paths)" means the five paths printed identical lines.

**PV-49 is new.** It was split out of PV-28: both verification lenses independently found and confirmed it while testing PV-28.

**PV-50 is post-audit.** Raised 2026-09-28 as an unprobed hypothesis, reproduced in the 2026-09-29/10-01 eager baselines, and resolved 2026-10-02: Model C supersedes its eager mechanism; Q-71 settles host admission at required units. Earlier lens verdicts remain history.

**PV-51 and PV-52 are post-fix records.** The Constitution audit (2026-10-23) recorded them from commit evidence, and each was already fixed when recorded: CACHE-OWNER-D2 and D1 (§ Resolved violations). They were never audit candidates, so they carry no lens verdicts.

**PV-53 and PV-54 are post-fix records too.** The Constitution catch-up (2026-11-15) recorded them from commit evidence (`da209fa0`, 2026-11-14), and each was already fixed when recorded (§ Resolved violations). The independent adversarial audit of 2026-11-14 found them; they were never candidates of the 2026-09-27 audit, so they carry no lens verdicts.

| PV-05 | `reduce([], {x + y}, 10 / randomInt(0, 2))` `--seed 5` (stream starts 0, 1) | `ok 10` (first draw 0 fails, retried draw succeeds); `take([], 10 / randomInt(0, 2))` → `DivisionByZero`; `reduce([], {x + y}, trace(1) / 0)` traces twice vs `contains` once |
| PV-06 | `G(x, y) = y` / `A = G({A}, randomInt(0, 1000000))` / `A` `--seed 1` | engine/generic/optimized `501906`; engineAsync/twin `853136` — **SUMMARY: DISAGREE** |
| PV-08 | `S((x)) = x` / `A = S` / `H(v) = S(v)` / `S([[7]]), H([[7]]), A([[7]])` | `S[L[7], L[7], 7]` — the alias opens one extra level |
| PV-12 | `F(0) = 5` / `F(n) = n * 10` / `repeat(F, 2, 1)` | `ArityMismatch` (engine and optimized), while `F(F(1)), F(0)` → `S[100, 5]` |
| PV-01 | see the Disputed entry | C# and Lean both `100101` |

The two PV-02 rows record the defect at `a2700f4`. On the fixed tree, both programs give their no-downloader result in both configurations: `S[100, 5]`, and `ArityMismatch` (§ Resolved violations).

The two PV-04 rows also record the defect at `a2700f4`. After the Q-01 decision, on the fixed tree over `3e57a08`, the first program is `DivisionByZero` with `host=[trace(1)]` and the second is `DivisionByZero` with `host=[tick#1]` — one evaluation of the failing argument, and no second value for the parameter — on all five paths (§ Resolved violations).

The PV-06 row records the defect at `a2700f4` as well. After the Q-02 decision every encountered resource limit is terminal, so that self-referential program can no longer succeed on any route: it fails with a resource-limit error whose kind may depend on the route. Its `self-reference` shape is pinned on the synchronous engine by `ResourceLimitTerminalityTests.TheLimitLaw_ALimitMayStopARunButNeverChangeItsValue`; the row was not re-run with the five-path runner (§ Resolved violations).

The PV-01 row records the behavior at `a2700f4`, which was not a violation of the rules as written. After the Q-04 decision, on the tree over `13196f8`, the program gives `3004`, the inlined helper's value, on all six routes of `AutomaticForwardingBindingTests`, and Lean evaluates the same elaborated tree to `3004` (spec case `forwarding-reuses-a-captured-ancestor-parameter`); see § Resolved violations.

The PV-05 row records the defect at `a2700f4` as well. After the builtin-adapter repair of 2026-09-29, on the tree over `515ed3c`, `reduce([], {x + y}, 10 / randomInt(0, 2))` with `--seed 5` is `DivisionByZero` and `reduce([], {x + y}, trace(1) / 0)` traces once, on all five paths; `take([], 10 / randomInt(0, 2))` is unchanged (§ Resolved violations).

The PV-03 row also records the defect at `a2700f4`. After the Q-03 decision, on the final fixed tree over `df3f8b0`, the same program with `--seed 7` gives `S[true, true, 571978, 571978, 571978]` on all five paths: every read of `Roll` is the one cached draw (§ Resolved violations).

The PV-08 row records the defect at `a2700f4`; it still reproduced at `bb0e543`. After the repair of 2026-09-29, on the tree over `bb0e543`, the program gives `S[L[7], L[7], L[7]]` on all five paths: the alias `A` is `S` for every argument (§ Resolved violations).

The PV-12 row records the behavior at `a2700f4`, which still reproduced through the morning of 2026-10-04 (worded since X-23). After the Q-23 decision, on the tree over `f6d978c`, the program gives `100` — the value of the direct `F(F(1))` — on all six routes, and Lean agrees (§ Resolved violations).

### Attack first

1. **PV-02, resolved 2026-09-28.** It was first on this list: a host setting (whether a downloader is configured) silently changed values, members, `open` provision and signatures of ordinary load-free source. The KatLangWeb playground always configures a downloader and its API validation never does, so the same public program could succeed in one and fail in the other. The fix was as small as predicted; see § Resolved violations.
2. **The retention and fall-through family: PV-04, PV-05, PV-19, PV-20.** In each, a retained or dropped slot failure takes a second route:
   - PV-04 was the direct #170 residual. User-call parameters re-ran a property body outside its cache entry, so one binding held several values and a seeded failure became a success depending on spelling. RESOLVED 2026-09-28: the owner decided Q-01 (at-most-once argument value evaluation, now CALL-06), and it was fixed in Lean and C# together (§ Resolved violations).
   - PV-05 turned failures into successes and gave 2^n CPU from a few hundred bytes of source.
   - PV-05, PV-19 and PV-20 concerned the BUILTIN adapter's own slots, which the Q-01 decision did not change. RESOLVED 2026-09-29, together, in Lean and C#, without a new decision: the collection-builtin adapter now handles each slot by its role — a value slot demanded once, a callback never value-evaluated, a failed spread the call's failure before arity (§ Resolved violations).
3. **PV-07 / Q-09, resolved 2026-10-04.** Q-02 had already settled terminality and PV-06 was resolved; the remaining choice — how strategy-selecting budgets may affect success versus resource-limit failure — was decided as Q-09 (Q-09a: host-stack headroom is host policy; Q-09b: limits never select a strategy), and PV-07 is fixed (§ Resolved violations). Reopen neither decision. *(Before 2026-10-04 this item read: "PV-07 / Q-09: remaining strategy and host-stack headroom … The current action is to decide how strategy-selecting budgets may affect success versus resource-limit failure; do not reopen the terminality decision.")*
   - PV-06 RESOLVED 2026-09-28: the owner decided Q-02 (every encountered resource-limit failure is terminal for the run), implemented in C# (§ Resolved violations).
   - PV-07 remained, narrowed: a non-binding budget could still select a strategy that stops with a resource-limit failure where the default configuration completes, but no longer turned one seeded success into another. Its remaining design choice was Q-09. *(Resolved 2026-10-04: no configured limit selects a strategy any more.)*
   - The same principle raised a new question: PV-50 / Q-71, a source-processing limit refusing a deferred module (still an ordinary, deferrable load error). *Re-baseline 2026-10-01:* reproduced by execution — in an ignored argument the refusal turns the seeded success `711` into `209`, and the module-count, aggregate-source and module-depth budgets and a missing module do the same (§ PV-50, Q-71).
4. **PV-03, resolved 2026-09-28, with PV-21 and PV-31.** Lifting positions versus the property cache was a real rule conflict between the September 22 "lifting unchanged" decision and the September 27 #170 law: PROP-04's own headline example (`Roll == Roll`) failed for a callable that PROP-04 declares eligible. The owner decided Q-03 (a callable that works with no arguments is read by its bare name; lifting skips it), and PV-03 and PV-27 are fixed (§ Resolved violations). PV-21 and PV-31 remain for callees that require arguments; their collecting-only witnesses no longer differ. *Since 2026-09-30:* PV-21 is resolved and PV-31 resolved by decision by the unified formula-lifting law (re-verified 2026-10-01).
5. **PV-08 and PV-11, both resolved 2026-09-29.** Both gave silent wrong values or silent signature changes, and neither can be seen by the Lean differential, because both are C# front-end mistakes accepted by both evaluators. Both are RESOLVED without a new decision: every open target is validated statically through one decomposition (PV-11), and implicit forwarding rebuilds a callee's sequence-value group from exactly the items its captures stand for (PV-08, FWD-02 amended); see § Resolved violations.
6. **Also needing decisions before release (current as of the 2026-10-01 re-baseline):**
   - PV-12 (Q-23; its false "no parameters" message should be fixed whatever Q-23 decides, X-23) — resolved 2026-10-04 (Q-23 decided; X-23 had fixed the message earlier that day);
   - PV-15 (the new Q-75) — resolved by decision 2026-10-05 (Q-75 decided);
   - PV-46 (Q-24) — resolved 2026-10-04 (Q-24 decided).
   PV-14 and PV-26, formerly listed here "decided together (which callables lift)", are resolved for formulas by the unified formula-lifting law (2026-09-30); only the lone-row alias/bare-forwarding eligibility of families (Q-13) and of non-Math builtins, host operations, opened and dotted members (Q-12) remains, as design questions. PV-24, PV-25 and PV-49, the small unambiguous fixes formerly listed here, were RESOLVED 2026-09-29 (§ Resolved violations). PV-27, formerly listed here too, was fixed by the Q-03 change.
7. **PV-01 (refuted as a violation; resolved by decision 2026-09-28).** The draft PAR-07 text had to be corrected, and the intent lens left an undecided design question that no test covered: implicit lifting could rebind a WRITTEN reference to an ancestor parameter. The owner decided it (Q-04: automatic parameter forwarding must not change what an existing name refers to), and the behavior changed; see § Resolved violations.

### PV-14 — Clause families get an empty callable signature, so a family reference is never lifted or forwarded — RESOLVED FOR FORMULAS 2026-09-30

- **2026-10-01 (the binding-indirection implementation):** implemented with X-47 — `F = Fact` dispatches as the family (`F(1, 2)` is `NoMatchingBranch`), a nameable family bare-forwards by its clause names, an unnameable family is aliasable, and a closed lone row into one is `UnforwardableCallable` (Q-77 resolved). This record's classification is unchanged.
- **2026-10-01 (the callable-capability investigation):** the lone-row remainder held by Q-13 is decided — a nameable family is a bare-forwarding target with no exact-alias contract, an unnameable family is neither; the C# implementation is pending (X-46) and the remaining row meanings are Q-77. This record's classification (resolved for its violation) is unchanged.
- **Re-baseline 2026-10-01 (post-lifting, `d6b88a9`; classification: RESOLVED for its violation, lone-row remainder transferred to Q-13):** `v01`, `v02` and `v05` give `7` on six routes; the same programs on the parent tree `4bea2e4` give `7`, `ArityMismatch` and `NoMatchingBranch`, so the change is exactly the unified law's. `m02` (`G(m) = sin(H)` with a family `H`) is now the closed-list front-end `UndeclaredIdentifier` naming `H` and `n`, as for any callee that requires an argument (formerly the runtime "No matching branch for 'H'"). Unnameable families are `UnliftableClauseFamily` with the reason (no plain binder at a position, disagreeing votes, or a name shared by two positions); a closed caller keeps the runtime demand. `v06` (`AliasG = G`) and the lone-row `UseG(n) = G` are unchanged (`ArityMismatch`, `NoMatchingBranch`): the lone-row facet has no settled oracle — FWD-02 excludes families from alias and bare-forwarding eligibility pending Q-13 — so it is Q-13's design question, not part of a live violation. The record is kept here for history; the resolved table carries the classification. Evidence: `post-lifting-rebaseline/probes/orig-witnesses/`, `probes/q13/`, `probes/matrices-prev-diff.txt`.

- **Resolved 2026-09-30 (the unified formula-lifting law (decided 2026-09-30: a formula lifts a reference exactly when its immediate consumer uses it as a VALUE and the callable it resolves to, whatever its category and route, has a lifting signature that requires supplied arguments)):** a clause family now has a lifting signature — one whole-value slot per top-level position, named by the plain binders of its clauses (literal, structural and binderless patterns vote nothing; votes must agree; positions need distinct names) — so the witnesses change as the law requires: `v01` and `v02` both give `7` (`UseG = G + 1` is `UseG(n) = G(n) + 1`; adding the base clause no longer changes the caller's arity), `v05` gives `7` (the closed caller's own `n` is forwarded by name), and a family whose clauses name no position is the targeted front-end error `UnliftableClauseFamily` where an inferring formula would lift it (never an invented name; a closed list keeps its runtime `NoMatchingBranch`). `v06` (the lone-row alias `AliasG = G`) is unchanged: alias and bare-forwarding eligibility is FWD-02's and stays open there (the alias half of Q-13). Callbacks (`v08`) are unchanged. Pinned by `UnifiedFormulaLiftingTests` and the spec cases `formula-lifting-is-one-law-for-every-callable` and `unliftable-clause-family`; re-run in `artifacts/validation/formula-lifting-law/rerun/` (family matrix: 42 changed programs, all as the law predicts). The record below is the audit's.

- **Constitution rule(s) at risk:**
  - PAR-07, which names no family exclusion;
  - PAT-11 ("an ordinary callable");
  - PAT-01, whose consequence table lacks this row;
  - FWD-02 (an alias means the call it abbreviates) and #114's expectation.
  - CALL-05 and RES-06 hold: the runtime NoMatchingBranch is the correct zero-argument outcome.
- **Status:** likely violation (both lenses).
- **Severity:** medium.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **What happens:**
  - `CallableSignature.FromAlgorithm` maps every Conditional to an empty signature, and every lifting gate tests `ps.Parameters.Count > 0`. So a family referenced bare in a lifting position is never rewritten into a forwarding call.
  - *Update 2026-09-28 (Q-03):* the lifting gates now ask `RequiresSuppliedArguments`, the zero-argument law over the callee's LIFTING signature, instead of `ps.Parameters.Count > 0`. A family's lifting signature is still empty, which that law accepts, so a family is still never lifted: `v01`, `v02`, `v05`, `v06` and `m02` give the same results on the fixed tree (`7`, `ArityMismatch`, `NoMatchingBranch`, `ArityMismatch`, `NoMatchingBranch`). The inversion below therefore stands. Q-03 did not decide Q-13; under the Q-03 rule a family, which from source always requires an argument, would become a lifting candidate once it has a lifting signature.
  - *Re-baseline 2026-09-29 (structural-pattern model):* unchanged. `v01`, `v02`, `v05`, `v06`, `v08` and `m02` give identical results with a CLI built from `bb0e543` and from the final tree (`artifacts/validation/structural-patterns/probes/rebaseline/pv14-*.kat`; `m02` names `H` rather than `radians` on BOTH trees — that label change predates this work). A family with list clauses is excluded the same way (`L([x, y]) = x + y` / `L(0) = 0` / `UseL = L + 1` / `UseL([1, 2])` → "Callable `UseL` expects 0 arguments"). The model removes one obstacle the PV-08 repro lens raised — a family's clause patterns now obey the same kind law as ordinary patterns (PAT-06), so FWD-02's same-kind reconstruction would suit a family's groups — but the naming question (a family has no single parameter-name list) is untouched, so PV-14 and Q-13 stand.
  - *Re-baseline 2026-09-29 (the alias and wrapper rules):* unchanged. A clause family is no alias or wrapper target (FWD-02's eligibility reads a parameter-pattern signature, which a family does not have), so `v01`, `v02`, `v05`, `v06`, `v08` and `m02` give identical results with a CLI built from `bb0e543` and from the final tree, and so does the lone-row wrapper `G(0) = 100` / `G(n) = n * 2` / `W(n) = G` / `W(3)` → "No matching branch for 'G'" (the family's bare zero-argument demand, like `v05`) — `artifacts/validation/alias-forwarding/probes/` `rebaseline.*`. The alias rule removes the naming obstacle for lone rows — an alias copies no binder names, and a WRAPPER of a family (`W(n) = G` as `G(n)`) needs no family signature at all — so a family wrapper is the smallest possible extension; it is not implemented (not decided). Formula lifting of a family would still need a naming rule, so PV-14 and Q-13 stand.
  - *Re-baseline 2026-09-30 (bare forwarding by name):* unchanged — `v01`, `v02`, `v05`, `v06`, `v08`, `m02` and the lone row `W(n) = G` give identical results with the CLI built from the positional tree and from the final tree (`artifacts/validation/bare-forwarding/probes/rebaseline-final.out`). The extension the previous note called the smallest is gone: bare forwarding is by NAME, so a family is a forwarding target only with a nameable family signature — the same naming question as a family alias and family formula lifting. PV-14 and Q-13 stand.
  - Adding one base clause changes the caller's arity: `UseG(3)` goes from 7 to "Callable `UseG` expects 0 arguments".
  - An alias of a family does not abbreviate it.
  - A closed caller's same-named parameter is not forwarded.
  - A strict Math position moves from a front-end UndeclaredIdentifier to a runtime "No matching branch for 'radians'", which names sin's internal parameter.
  - This inverts the runtime's own classification (`AcceptsZeroSuppliedArguments` says a family NEEDS arguments). Every failure is loud; no silent wrong value was found.
- **Minimal probe:** `probes/PV-14-verify/v01.kat` against `v02.kat`:
  ```
  G(n) = n * 2
  UseG = G + 1
  UseG(3)
  ```
  ```
  G(0) = 100
  G(n) = n * 2
  UseG = G + 1
  UseG(3)
  ```
  `v05.kat` (the `v02` family with `Outer(n) = G + 1` / `Outer(3)`), `v06.kat` (`AliasG = G` / `AliasG(3)`), `v08.kat` (`map([0, 3], G)`), and `m02.kat`:
  ```
  H(0) = 1
  H(n) = n * 2
  G(m) = sin(H)
  G(1)
  ```
- **Observed output:**
  ```
  v01: [engine] ok 7 n=1                                                                  SUMMARY: AGREE (all 5 paths)
  v02: [engine] err ArityMismatch @[4:1, 4:8): Callable `UseG` expects 0 arguments, but was called with 1 argument.   SUMMARY: AGREE
  v05: [engine] err NoMatchingBranch @[3:12, 3:13): while evaluating call to Outer: No matching branch for 'G'      SUMMARY: AGREE
  v06: [engine] err ArityMismatch @[4:1, 4:10): Callable `AliasG` expects 0 arguments, but was called with 1 argument.  SUMMARY: AGREE
  v08: [engine] ok L[100, 6] n=1                                                          SUMMARY: AGREE
  m02: [engine] err NoMatchingBranch @[3:8, 3:14): while evaluating call to G: while evaluating call to sin: No matching branch for 'radians'   SUMMARY: AGREE
  ```
- **Code paths involved:**
  - `src/KatLang/Signatures/CallableSignature.cs:160-166` (`Algorithm.Conditional => new CallableSignature(name, [])` at `:165`).
  - `src/KatLang/ImplicitArgumentResolver.cs`:
    - `:907-914` and `:1066` (signature map);
    - `:2260`/`:2271`, `:1974` and `:1391-1398` (gates).
  - Contrast: `src/KatLang/Evaluator.cs:1219-1225` `AcceptsZeroSuppliedArguments` (the family arm uses the real branch arity).
  - Lean: `lean/KatLang.lean:1699-1712` (params and signature `[]` for `.conditional`); `:7146-7152` lifting comment.
  - Only the representation is pinned: `tests/KatLang.Tests/CallableBindingPlanParityTests.cs:715-738`, `AlgorithmParameterNamesTests.cs:58-68`.
- **Lean behavior:** Lean does not model lifting. On the elaborated tree it agrees with C#: `v02` arity, `v05` branch, `v07` arity.
- **Verifier notes:**
  - Both lenses rate it a likely violation, not confirmed.
  - The plausible design reason is that forwarding is by NAME, and a family has no single parameter-name list (`G(0)` binds no name).
  - It should be decided together with PV-26 ("which callables lift").
- **Recommendation:** decide design question. Either give families a lifting signature (uniform arity plus a naming rule), or state the exclusion in PAR-07, PAT-01 and PAT-11 and replace the silent path with a targeted front-end diagnostic.

### PV-21 — Operands nested inside a dot receiver are lifted, while the same expression as a call argument is never lifted at any depth, so `R.F` ≢ `F(R)` through elaboration — RESOLVED 2026-09-30

- **Re-baseline 2026-10-01 (post-lifting, `d6b88a9`; classification: RESOLVED, direct):** `c1` (`K(x) = Id(A + 0)`) and `c2` (`K(x) = (A + 0).Id`) both give `2`; `i2` gives `2` and `i4` `1` (all `ArityMismatch` on the parent tree `4bea2e4`); `c4` gives `S[0, 0, 0, 1, 1]`. Both the fallback case (`(A + 0).Id` ≡ `Id(A + 0)`: the selected fallback is the call slot by slot) and the neutral whole argument (`A.Id` ≡ `Id(A)`: a user callable's whole argument keeps the reference) follow the same role law, and structural navigation (`Lib.M + 0`, the navigated receiver) keeps its distinct role. Evidence: `post-lifting-rebaseline/probes/orig-witnesses/`, `probes/q11/`.

- **Resolved 2026-09-30 (the unified formula-lifting law (decided 2026-09-30: a formula lifts a reference exactly when its immediate consumer uses it as a VALUE and the callable it resolves to, whatever its category and route, has a lifting signature that requires supplied arguments)):** the role is the immediate consumer's and RECURSIVE, so an expression nested in any argument takes its own consumer's role, and a selected fallback `R.F(args)` is the call `F(R, args)` slot by slot: `K(x) = (A + 0).Id` and `K(x) = Id(A + 0)` now agree, as do both spellings of every witness (`c1`, `c2`), and `(A + 1).string` lifting is now the stated rule (the `.string` receiver is a value position). A user callable's WHOLE argument stays neutral (sub-choice A1), so `Id(A)` still passes `A` itself. Re-run in `artifacts/validation/formula-lifting-law/rerun/` (dot-equivalence: 14 changed programs, every implicit spelling now equal to its explicit twin). The record below is the audit's.

- **Constitution rule(s) at risk:**
  - DOT-03 (value, error kind, caching and effects of `R.F` equal those of `F(R)`);
  - AGENTS ("Dotted-call equivalence is uniform through frontend elaboration");
  - sequences-lists-and-calls.md:7 (a dot-call receiver is a position "the resolver never lifts in any caller");
  - ownership-and-lookup.md:52;
  - PAR-07, whose sentence says the `.string` receiver never lifts "even for operands nested inside them", which is false.
  - RAND-01 is affected only downstream.
- **Status:** confirmed violation (both lenses).
- **Severity:** low–medium. The repro lens rated it low; the intent lens rated it medium because of a silent-value witness.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **What happens:**
  - `RewriteDotCall` rewrites the receiver with `inCallPosition: true`. That protects only a bare top-level name: the Binary, Comparison, Unary, Index, List and Math-call arms beneath it lift.
  - Call arguments go through `ProcessArgumentBundle`/`ProcessExprNested`, which never lift.
  - Under a closed list, `K(x) = (A + 0).Id` succeeds while `K(x) = Id(A + 0)` fails.
  - With a collecting-only helper both spellings succeed with DIFFERENT values: `Show(Total * 2)` is 0 while `(Total * 2).Show` is 12.
  - *Update 2026-09-28 (Q-03):* a collecting-only helper is no longer lifted in any position, so this silent-value witness is gone: on the fixed tree `c4` gives `S[0, 0, 0, 1, 1]`, both spellings `0`. The violation stands for callees that require arguments: `c1` and `c2` are unchanged.
  - `(A + 1).string` lifts, although PAR-07 says it does not.
- *Re-baseline 2026-09-29 (structural-pattern model):* unchanged — `c1`, `c2` and `c4` give identical results with a CLI built from `bb0e543` and from the final tree (`artifacts/validation/structural-patterns/probes/rebaseline/pv21-*.kat`). The finding concerns lifting positions, which the structural-pattern model does not touch.
- *Re-baseline 2026-09-29 (the alias and wrapper rules):* unchanged — `c1`, `c2` and `c4` give identical results with a CLI built from `bb0e543` and from the final tree (`artifacts/validation/alias-forwarding/probes/` `rebaseline.*`). Every witness uses its callee inside an argument or a receiver, which is formula lifting; the alias rule concerns only a body whose one row is the bare callee.
- *Re-baseline 2026-09-30 (bare forwarding by name):* unchanged — `c1`, `c2` and `c4` give identical results (`artifacts/validation/bare-forwarding/probes/rebaseline-final.out`); every witness is formula lifting, which the final decision does not touch.
- **Minimal probe:** `probes/PV-21-verify/c1.kat` against `c2.kat`:
  ```
  A = x + 1
  Id(v) = v
  K(x) = Id(A + 0)
  K(1)
  ```
  ```
  A = x + 1
  Id(v) = v
  K(x) = (A + 0).Id
  K(1)
  ```
  `probes/PV-21-mech/c4.kat`:
  ```
  Total(*items) = sum(items)
  Show(v) = v
  R1(*items) = Show(Total * 2)
  R2(*items) = (Total * 2).Show
  R3(*items) = Total * 2
  R4(*items) = sum([Total, 1])
  R5(*items) = [Total, 1].sum
  R1(1, 2, 3), R2(1, 2, 3), R3(1, 2, 3), R4(1, 2, 3), R5(1, 2, 3)
  ```
- **Observed output:**
  ```
  c1: [engine] err ArityMismatch @[3:11, 3:12): while evaluating call to K: while evaluating call to Id: Property 'A' expects 1 parameter, but was called with 0 arguments.   SUMMARY: AGREE (all 5 paths)
  c2: [engine] ok 2 n=1                          SUMMARY: AGREE
  c4: [engine] ok S[0, 12, 12, 1, 7] n=5         SUMMARY: AGREE
  ```
- **Code paths involved:**
  - `src/KatLang/ImplicitArgumentResolver.cs`:
    - `:2344-2362` `RewriteDotCall` (target at `:2355`);
    - `:2181-2220` (operand arms, which lift);
    - `:2320-2331` `RewriteCall` → `:2404-2408` `ProcessArgumentBundle` → `:2517-2597` `ProcessExprNested` (never lifts);
    - `CollectImplicitDeps` `:2044-2062` (target `:2056`) against `:1999-2008`.
  - `src/KatLang/PropertyDependencyGraph.cs:2619-2645` against `:2560-2579`, which mirror the same split.
  - Lean does not model lifting: `lean/KatLang.lean:7146-7192` is a comment.
- **Lean behavior:** Lean agrees on the derived AST: `c1` arity in both, `c2` 2 in both, `c4` S[0, 12, 12, 1, 7] in both. The divergence enters in the C# front end, before either evaluator runs.
- **Verifier notes:**
  - Both lenses confirmed the violation.
  - Repro: unifying in either direction changes behaviour that works today, so this is a decision.
  - Intent: make a must-selected non-Math fallback receiver a neutral argument slot, per the documented intent. The silent witness also needs PV-03's lifting of collecting-only callables (PV-03 is resolved, so that witness no longer reproduces; see the update above).
- **Recommendation:** decide design question. Then make receiver lifting and argument lifting identical, and correct PAR-07's `.string` sentence.

### PV-26 — Only Math aliases are lifted: aliases of non-Math builtins and host operations (`C = count`, `T = trace`) become zero-parameter properties — FORMULA HALF RESOLVED 2026-09-30; RESOLVED as a violation 2026-10-01, lone-row remainder transferred to Q-12

- **2026-10-01 (the binding-indirection implementation):** implemented with X-47 — `C = count`, `T = trace` and opened, dotted and module members are callable aliases with their target's own invocation; non-Math builtins bare-forward by their registry names (`A(collection) = count` / `A([1, 2])` is `2`). This record's classification is unchanged.
- **2026-10-01 (the callable-capability investigation):** the lone-row remainder held by Q-12 is decided — host operations and opened, dotted and module members are alias and bare-forwarding targets, non-Math builtins are bare-forwarding targets with no exact-alias contract; the C# implementation is pending (X-46) and `C = count`'s meaning is Q-77. This record's classification is unchanged.
- **Re-baseline 2026-10-01 (post-lifting, `d6b88a9`; classification: RESOLVED for its violation, lone-row remainder transferred to Q-12):** in a FORMULA every category lifts — `C = count + 0` is `C(collection)` (`2`), `if + 0`, `repeat + 0`, `[take]:0`, `trace + 0` (one trace), `hpair + 0`, an opened `Inc + 0` (inside a block or under a root `open`) and the dotted `Lib.Inc + 0` all take their callee's parameters; the parent tree `4bea2e4` gives `ArityMismatch` for every one. The LONE rows are unchanged: `k01` (`C = count`), `k02` (`T = trace`), `C = if`, `C = repeat`, the opened `C = Inc`, the dotted `C = Lib.Inc` and `u08` (`map(…, C)`) give `ArityMismatch`, and the closed lone rows `C(collection) = count`, `C(x) = trace`, `C(x) = Inc`, `C(x) = Lib.Inc` read the bare callee (its own zero-argument rejection), while user properties and Math members alias and bare-forward (`u01`, `u11`, `k04`, `C(x) = sqrt` → `3`, `C(value) = sqrt` → `UnforwardableParameter`). FWD-02 states that eligibility explicitly as "unchanged … pending Q-12", so the remainder has no settled oracle: it is Q-12's design question, and PV-26 is no longer counted as an active violation. Evidence: `post-lifting-rebaseline/probes/q12/`, `probes/orig-witnesses/`, `probes/matrices-prev-diff.txt`.

- **Formula half resolved 2026-09-30 (the unified formula-lifting law (decided 2026-09-30: a formula lifts a reference exactly when its immediate consumer uses it as a VALUE and the callable it resolves to, whatever its category and route, has a lifting signature that requires supplied arguments)):** builtins (`ToolingPlainSignature`: `count(collection)`, `if(condition, whenTrue, whenFalse)`, `repeat(step, count, *init)`), host operations (the resolver now receives the run's host operations) and dotted and opened members lift in a FORMULA exactly like the Math aliases: `C = count + 0` / `C((1, 2))` gives `2`, `T = trace + 0` / `T(7)` gives `7` with one trace. The lone rows `k01` (`C = count` / `C((1, 2))`) and `T = trace` are unchanged — still `ArityMismatch` — because a lone row is FWD-02's and its eligibility deliberately stays as it was (the alias half of Q-12, still open there). The record below is the audit's.

- **Constitution rule(s) at risk:**
  - RES-06 and AGENTS SYN-05 (builtins and host operations are ordinary prelude bindings);
  - ownership-and-lookup.md:52 and the AstHelpers.cs:287 docstring ("owner-walk properties lift (the alias `sin` is a prelude property)"), which state a route-based principle that `count` and `trace` satisfy;
  - FWD-02's rationale, and #114.
  - As drafted, PAR-07 and FWD-02 carve this case out. HO-01 and COLL-01 are not violated.
- **Status:** likely violation (both lenses).
- **Severity:** low.
- **Confidence:** medium–high. The repro lens rated confidence medium; the intent lens rated it high.
- **What happens:**
  - `RewriteBareReference` lifts only declared properties with parameters and registry-proven Math aliases. Non-Math builtins and host operations never enter the resolver's signature map, and the resolver is not even given the configured host operations.
  - So `C = count` / `C((1, 2))` and `T = trace` / `T(7)` fail with "Callable `C` expects 0 arguments", and `map(xs, C)` fails.

    - an alias of a USER property named `count`;
    - an alias of a user wrapper of `count`.

- *Re-baseline 2026-09-29 (structural-pattern model):* unchanged — `k01`, `u11`, `k04`, `u01` and `u08` give identical results with a CLI built from `bb0e543` and from the final tree (`artifacts/validation/structural-patterns/probes/rebaseline/pv26-*.kat`; `k02` needs a host `trace` operation and was not re-run). Builtin aliases carry no structural pattern, so the model cannot affect them.
- *Re-baseline 2026-09-29 (the alias and wrapper rules):* unchanged — `k01`, `u11`, `k04`, `u01` and `u08` give identical results on both trees (`artifacts/validation/alias-forwarding/probes/` `rebaseline.*`). A non-Math builtin or host operation is no alias or wrapper target (FWD-02's eligibility), so `C = count` stays a zero-parameter property, while the Math alias `S = abs` (`k04`) and the user-property aliases (`u01`, `u11`) are now exact aliases with the same results. The disparity PV-26 records is unchanged; it is now a question of alias-target eligibility (Q-12).
- *Re-baseline 2026-09-30 (bare forwarding by name):* unchanged — `k01`, `u11`, `k04`, `u01` and `u08` give identical results (`artifacts/validation/bare-forwarding/probes/rebaseline-final.out`). A non-Math builtin or host operation is still no alias or forwarding target, so the disparity and Q-12 stand.
