#### Q-36 — Only a spread operand's OWN missing output becomes `SpreadMissingOutput`? (X-29; EFF-06) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-24 (spread preserves nested failures and their blame; implemented)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-24 (owner decision accepted 2026-10-24); implemented in Lean and C# together, with regression, differential and diagnostic coverage. Resolves X-29.
- **The decision:** *Spread preserves failures originating within its operand's dependencies or arguments, including their category, cause, and blame. Only the operand's own missing output becomes `SpreadMissingOutput`. The spread site may add diagnostic context.* Direct missing output — the computation the operand directly denotes or invokes has no output (`{}*`, `G*`, `G()*`, and through parameter forwarding `P(x) = x*` / `P({})`) — is `SpreadMissingOutput`; a nested failure — in a dependency, argument, output row, constructed value, operator operand, builtin argument or callback, inspected argument or intrinsic receiver (`H = G + 1` / `H*`, `H()*`, `F({})*`, `{ G }*`, `(G, 1)*`, `[G]*`) — keeps its category, cause, frames and location under one added `SpreadOperandContext` frame; empty values and supplies (`()*`, `[]*`, `{ []* }*`) are not missing output; other kinds and an inner spread's own report pass unchanged.
- **Why:** the former rewrite made a failure's kind depend on an enclosing construct (FORMAL-06's innermost category), reported "the spread operand has no defined output" for operands that have output, and dropped F5's written-argument blame.
- **Mechanism:** provenance on the completed failure — Lean `Error.missingOutput : MissingOutputOrigin → Error`, C# the equality-transparent `EvalError.MissingOutput.IsNested` — raised `own` by the demanded computation's output check and nested at every subordinate boundary (Lean `withNestedMissingOutput`; C# `NestMissingOutput`, copying, never mutating a memoized failure). The spread's decision reads it and evaluates nothing, so the origin survives property caches and need cells for every consumer.
- **Rules:** SUP-02, RUN-07, VAL-10 (translation caveat), the CALL F5 note; FORMAL-06 unchanged. Tracked docs: `sequences-lists-and-calls.md` § Spread failure origin, `evaluator-and-hosting.md` § Blame for an output-less written argument, `SEMANTIC-ALIGNMENT.md` (X-29 / Q-36 entry).
- **Evidence:** Lean `CoreTests/SpreadFailureOrigin.lean`; C# `SpreadFailureOriginTests`, `BuiltinArgumentRoleTests.FailedSpread_PropagatesItsOwnFailure`; nineteen explorer `spread*` specials; spec case `spread-preserves-nested-missing-output`; validation report under `artifacts/validation/q36/`.

#### Q-37 — The re-entrant read of a zero-parameter property (EFF-07; CB-09) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-11 (the outermost successful property-style evaluation of a key owns its entry)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-11. The owner adopted outermost ownership of the cache entry; Lean and C# changed together.
- **The decision:** *the OUTERMOST successful property-style evaluation of a cache key owns its entry.* (1) A property-style read that misses while no evaluation of the same key is running is the key's owner; the key is active until the owner finishes, on every exit. (2) A read of the same key while it is active — directly (`A → A`), through other properties and calls (`A → B → A`), or beneath an explicit call's frame — is re-entrant: it evaluates the body and returns its own, possibly intermediate, result, and publishes nothing. (3) Only the owner's success is published, every later ordinary read reuses it, and publication never replaces an entry. (4) A failed owner publishes nothing for its key — no same-key re-entrant result computed during the failed attempt becomes the entry — while entries other keys' owners published stay. (5) An explicit `A()` is never an owner *(Constitution audit, 2026-10-23: clause (5) was superseded on 2026-10-22 by CACHE-PUB-1 (#189, `586f32f3`). A qualifying zero-supply `A()` that finds the key empty and inactive is its owner and establishes the entry, so the witness `A(), A` is now `S[2, 2]`; see decision-lineages.md § CACHE-PUB-1 explicit zero-supply calls establish the property cache, PROP-06, PROP-09)*. Intermediate re-entrant results may differ from the published one; the guarantee is that ordinary reads after the owner's success agree.
- **Why:** under the first-successful-completion rule (`31f7c76`, 2026-09-12) the innermost re-entrant completion finished first and was stored, so the read that started a recursive evaluation returned one value and every later read another (`S[2, 0]`). The owner decided that the value of a binding is the value its own (outermost) evaluation produced — neither of the two options this row recorded (return the stored first entry to the outermost read too, or document the disagreement).
- **Witnesses (six C# routes, 2026-10-11; Lean on hand-built trees):** `A = if(tick() < 3, A + 1, 0)` / `A, A` → `S[2, 2]` after three ticks (formerly `S[2, 0]`); the seeded `Classify`/`tick` reproduction with seed 7 → `2`, `2` after exactly three draws; `A = if(tick() < 3, A + A, 1)` / `A, A` → `S[3, 3]` after five ticks; `A = if(tick() < 3, B + 1, 0)` / `B = A + 1` / `A, A, B, B` → `S[4, 4, 3, 3]`; `A(), A` → `S[2, 1]`; a failing owner after an inner same-key success publishes nothing, while another key's owner keeps its entry. Lean (`CoreTests/PropertyCachePublication.lean`): `P = if(x == 0, 1, G(x - 1) + 100)` / `G(x) = P` / `G(1), G(5)` → `S[101, 101]` (formerly `S[101, 1]`), with the same values on the C# routes.
- **Rules:** PROP-09 (title, status, rule, why, examples, boundary, tension, evidence; rule-index row), PROP-04 (the reuse sentence, boundary, tension), VAL-10 (surviving-state bullet and example); the PROP topic item; Appendix A P01, P35 and Q22.
- **Evidence:** `../q37-outermost-property-cache/implementation-report.md`, `semantic-contract.md`, `tests-and-validation.md`, `constitution-changes.md`, `preservation.md`.

#### Q-45 — The evaluation order of `.string(args)` (oq DOT-03; PV-38) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-10 (the current Model-C order is the law: formation, then cardinality, then the receiver)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-10. The owner kept the current Model-C behavior as intended and closed the question; no C# or Lean behavior changed.
- **The decision:** *the `.string` intrinsic accepts exactly zero supplied arguments, and its behavior follows the ordinary Model-C rules.* (1) Written argument supplies are formed. (2) Explicit arbitrary spreads execute during supply formation. (3) Ordinary non-spread supplied computations remain suspended. (4) The intrinsic rejects a nonzero supplied argument count with `ArityMismatch`, before demanding the receiver or any ordinary argument. (5) If the resulting supply has zero arguments, the intrinsic demands the receiver's VALUE and converts it to its numeric string representation. (6) Extension fallback calls follow their own ordinary demand semantics (DOT-03); there is no universal special receiver-first rule. There is no special argument-first evaluation rule for `.string`.
- **Why:** the question was formulated against the pre-Model-C order — the written arguments evaluated before, and instead of, the receiver, while extension fallback was receiver-first. Model C (2026-10-02; NEED-01, NEED-03, NEED-05) removed both halves of that premise: a supplied computation runs only when demanded and cardinality precedes every non-spread demand, so a rejected `.string(args)` evaluates neither its receiver nor its ordinary arguments, while an extension fallback demands its receiver like any argument, in its callee's order. The Phase A2 re-run (2026-10-09) recorded this and left the decision to the owner, who accepted it as the law. RUN-08 lists the `.string` receiver with its closed set of demand points.
- **Witnesses (six C# routes, re-run 2026-10-10; Lean agreeing on trace-free twins):** `trace(5).string(trace(6))` → `ArityMismatch`, no host event; `trace(5).string([trace(6)]*)` → `ArityMismatch` after `trace(6)` only; `trace(5).string(trace(())*)` → `'5'`, host log `[trace(S[]), trace(5)]`; `trace(5).string` and `trace(5).string()` → `'5'`, host log `[trace(5)]`. Lean (`CoreTests/Strings.lean` § Q-45): `(1 / 0).string(1 / 0)` and `{ 1 / 0 }.string(1 / 0)` → `arityMismatch 0 1`; `(1 / 0).string([2]*)` → `arityMismatch 0 1`; `42.string([1 / 0]*)` → `divByZero`; `(1 / 0).string([not 1]*)` → the spread's `typeMismatch`; `42.string(()*)` → `'42'`, while `(1 / 0).string(()*)` and `{ 1 / 0 }.string()` → `divByZero`.
- **Rules:** DOT-08 (status; **Arguments**; the Q-28 consequence sentence; examples; tension; evidence; the DOT topic item), RUN-08 (the `.string` receiver as a demand point; the explicit-spread strictness), DOT-03 (unchanged: extension fallback's demand order); PV-38 resolved by decision; Appendix A P11 and Q42.
- **Evidence:** `../q45-string-args-resolution/final-report.md`; the Phase A2 re-run `../constitution-model-c-a2-reconciliation/witness-results.md`.

#### Q-25 — The single-value result contract of `map`/`reduce` (X-32; oq VAL-01) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-10 (Option B: a callback returns its ordinary call result)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-10. The owner adopted the investigation's recommendation, Option B (`../q25-callback-result-investigation/final-report.md`, verdict DECISION READY) — the record's option (b).
- **The decision:** *a `map` transform or `reduce` step returns the ordinary result of calling its callback.* Multi-row output becomes one sequence value; `()` and `[]` are valid results; `map` stores the complete result as ONE element and `reduce` passes it as ONE accumulator; there is no implicit spread and no cardinality or non-empty restriction. Errors propagate normally and `MissingOutput` is preserved; `filter` keeps its Boolean requirement and loop-step row semantics are unchanged. Option A (keep the strict contract) and option C (reject only `()`) were not adopted.
- **Why:** after ordinary calls became value boundaries, retaining the raw-output callback restriction broke compositionality, identity mapping and wrapper equivalence. The superseded contract — #37's single-value result (2026-04-08), kept by #132 and #135 and extended to clause families by D1 (2026-10-09) — is preserved as history (`decision-lineages.md` § Q-25 — owner decision and implementation — 2026-10-10).
- **Laws:** `map(L, F) ≡ [F(L[0]), …, F(L[n-1])]` and `reduce([a, b], R, i) ≡ R(b, R(a, i))` in result value for pure, deterministic, total computations; wrapper invariance (`D(x) = x, x`, `G(x) = D(x)` and `H(x) = (x, x)` all map `[1]` to `[(1, 1)]`); the identity map (`map([(), 1, [], 2], Id)` is `[(), 1, [], 2]`); accumulator closure (`R(x, acc) = x, acc` gives `(2, (1, 0))`, and `R(x, acc) = acc` over the initial `()` gives `()`); the next accumulator carries the ordinary value-boundary count. The #203 and #204 demand qualifications are in HO-02 and HO-03. A fold reads the collection's top level first, then follows nested VALUE demands of its accumulators. A mapped position reads its source before invoking the transform.
- **Implementation (2026-10-10, working tree over `main` @ `c74cd117`):** Lean deletes `expectSingleValueWith`, `expectSingleAccumulator` and `expectSingleMappedElement`; `evalNeedUserSupply` and `evalNeedFamilySupply` lose their `recount` argument and always end at `reCountValueBoundary`; `evalMapCounted`, `evalReduceCounted` and `evalFilterCounted` invoke through the previously unused `evalSequenceCallbackCallCounted` / `evalSequenceReduceStepCounted` / `evalSequenceCallbackCall`. C# deletes `ExpectSingleEmittedValue` and its two wrappers; `EvalMapCounted` / `EvalReduceCounted` and their async twins store and thread the call result whole; the `recount` flag of `EvalNeedUserSupply*`, which doubled as the variadic arity-diagnostic style, is separated into `variadicArityStyle`, and `EvalNeedFamilySupply*` lose theirs. The optimizer needed no change.
- **Witnesses (six routes, Lean agreeing):** the 92-program investigation matrix (`CallbackResultBoundaryTests.InvestigationMatrix`), e.g. `map([()], Id)` → `L[S[]]` (formerly `ArityMismatch`), `D(x) = x, x` / `map([1], D)` → `L[S[1, 1]]`, `R(x, acc) = x, acc` / `reduce([1, 2], R, 0)` → `S[2, S[1, 0]]`, `Lib = { public V = 1 }` / `F(x) = Lib` / `map([1], F)` → `MissingOutput` (unchanged), `P(x) = x > 1, x < 5` / `filter([2], P)` → `TypeMismatch` (unchanged). Compatibility of every baseline-valid program: `../q25-callback-result-investigation/implementation/compatibility.md`.
- **Rules:** HO-03 (rewritten), HO-02, HO-04, HO-05, VAL-04, VAL-06, VAL-08, SEQ-04, COLL-04, PAT-11, LOOP-07, FORMAL-05, Appendix A.

#### Q-33 — RESOLVED; conflicting line-final subrule revised 2026-10-14 (refined again by issue #183 the same day)

> **Refinement (issue #183, owner decision 2026-10-14):** the line-final subrule restated below was refined the same day: attachment classifies a line-final star — attached `A*` is a spread that completes the expression, detached `A *` is multiplication (current SYN-11). The bullets below are the Q-65 formulation and are history wherever they conflict (the EOF, attached-newline and root-final `Values*` statements).

**Rule:** Prefix attached `*name` is collect in binding positions, infix `*` is multiplication, and directly attached postfix `expr*` is spread only with explicit same-line slot closure. No new syntax or spread VALUE semantics is introduced.

- A physical line-final star has multiplication priority, attached or spaced. `7*` newline `8` and `7 *` newline `8` give 56. EOF is not a spread boundary: `7*` at EOF is a missing multiplication operand. A later declaration or closer cannot turn it into spread.
- `7*` newline `X = 8` reports the dangling multiplication and preserves X. Comments and blank lines do not manufacture a spread boundary; declarations are never operands (SYN-10).
- Explicit same-line comma, closing delimiter, fluent dot or a closed chained-spread layer permits spread: `F(A*)`, `[A*]`, `Data[Indexes*]`, `A*, B`, `A*.F`, `(A**)`. Spread supplies one item-producing boundary; capture, lists, calls and root output consume it under their existing laws.
- Classification precedes attachment: `F(A *)` is InvalidSpreadMarker; multiplication spacing remains ordinary. Prefix collect and Grace keep their exact attachment rules (SYN-12).
- Leading star can continue multiplication under SYN-08 grammar priority; a collecting declaration remains independent. Arithmetic precedence, chained-spread composition, fluent same-line lowering and collect/spread VALUE semantics are unchanged.
- Root-final bare `Values*` is intentionally no longer valid. Use an explicitly closed receiver or a same-line comma followed by a real output. A capture/brace creates one value and does not preserve root row cardinality. Definition bodies ending in spread use same-line closure, `X = (A*)` or `X = { A* }`.


The original 2026-10-09 resolution and its earlier evidence remain historical below and in decision-lineages.md. Only its conflicting line-final/EOF fallback is superseded; prefix collect, attachment-after-classification, multiplication precedence and spread VALUE semantics are retained.

#### Q-16 — Grace (X-08, X-39; oq LIFT-10) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-07 (G-O: owner-local Grace)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-07. The owner adopted G-O, owner-local Grace — the recommendation of the investigation `../q16-grace-investigation/final-report.md` (worktree `q16-grace-ownership-81ee86`, verdict DECISION READY): Q-16(1) **E** (eligibility, not actual movement) and Q-16(2) **O** (nested inferred owners retain their own Grace). The question is closed; X-08 and X-39 are resolved, PV-28 is resolved by decision, and oq LIFT-10 is closed (part 1 by X-39, part 2 by X-08).
- **The decision (PAR-06, PAT-04):** *Grace belongs to the owner whose written rows contain the marked occurrence. A marker is valid exactly when that occurrence becomes one of the owner's OWN inferred parameters. Its weight is applied as far as the ordering allows; saturation is never an error.* The owner is the innermost algorithm-level scope — the root, a property body, a brace block in any expression position, a clause-branch body — whose output rows or deconstruction right-hand sides (`AstHelpers.WrittenRows`) contain the occurrence, through every transparent construct; hoisting never moves an occurrence to another owner.
  - (1) "Effective" means ELIGIBLE: `F = ~x + 1`, an already-first `~x`, an already-last `x~`, excess weight, a tie, a cancelled weight and a marker blocked by the lifted tail (`A = p - q` / `F = A - z~` is `F(z, p, q)`) are valid. A marker on a fixed binding — an explicit parameter or clause binder, an enclosing parameter, a visible property, a builtin, an opened name, a structural member, `.string` — or on any occurrence of a closed level (a written list; a clause branch's own level) stays `InvalidGraceMarker`: a fixed binding has no inferred parameter for the weight to attach to, while a saturated free name has one. Adding or removing an unrelated own parameter never changes whether a marker is legal.
  - (2) A clause branch is closed at its own level only. A nested algorithm — a brace block in any position, a property, a nested family's nested owners, at any depth — that infers its own signature owns its Grace exactly like any owner: `Apply(f) = f(1, 10)` / `F(0) = Apply({ y - ~x })` / `F(0)` gives `9`, like the named `F(0) = { B = y - ~x ⏎ Apply(B) }`. A branch binder seen from a nested owner is an enclosing parameter (`F(n) = Apply({ x - ~n })` stays `InvalidGraceMarker`, reported once); nothing is lifted into the branch; adding a sibling clause never changes a nested owner's verdict; a definition body written as ONE brace block IS the branch body (`G(k) = { y - ~x }` is the branch's own level).
- **Rejected alternatives:** M (movement required: its five formalizations disagree pairwise and reject saturated markers that canonical cases pin), L (a lexical branch ban: six boundary clauses and three spelling escapes), and the former hybrid (X-08's inline/named split).
- **Canonical examples (six routes):** `F = ~x + 1` / `F(3)` → `4`; `A = p - q` / `F = A - z~` / `F(1, 2, 3)` → `-2`; `F = y - ~x` / `F(1, 10)` → `9`; `F(x) = ~x + 1` → `InvalidGraceMarker` ("Grace cannot reorder 'x' because it already resolves to an explicit parameter …"); `Apply(f) = f(1, 10)` / `F(0) = Apply({ y - ~x })` / `F(0)` → `9`, and the named property spelling → `9`; `Apply(f) = f(1)` / `F(0) = 0` / `F(n) = Apply({ x - ~n })` → `InvalidGraceMarker` ("… a parameter of an enclosing algorithm"), one report.
- **Compatibility (`../q16-grace-implementation/compatibility.md`; 653 probe variants on six routes, baseline `66367a66` against the candidate):** no accepted program is rejected; no signature, value or host-call change for any program accepted before and after; 87 rejected programs are accepted — every one rejected at the baseline only by the parser's lexical branch scan on a nested owner's own marker (one of them through module text, formerly `InvalidLoadedSource`), and one of them, a load-bearing branch, now reports its own-level marker when the deferred unit is selected; diagnostics: 20 duplicate reports removed (same span), 8 order changes (the Grace report is now a detector diagnostic, after the parser's), 88 message-only rewordings.
- **Implementation (2026-10-07, working tree over `main` @ `66367a66`):** `Parser.cs` — the clause-group branch-body Grace scan and its iterative traversal (`FindGraceSpan` / `ScanPendingForGraceSpan`, a runtime-guarded `Expr` walk) are deleted; the parser keeps Grace syntax only. `ParameterDetector.cs` — `GraceEffectPolicy.ClosedBranch` replaces `NotReported` (the branch region passes it with its own level); `DescribeFixedGraceBinding` names a clause binder and a branch's own level; `FormatIneffectiveGrace` words every report as eligibility ("Grace cannot reorder 'x' because …"). `CollectFreeParams` and `ApplyGraceReordering` are unchanged (the X-49 witness keeps `K(a, c, b)`). No evaluator, resolver, Lean-semantics, grammar or public-API change; the Lean `Pattern`, `CondBranch` and `Algorithm.conditional` docstrings are narrowed to the branch's own level (comments only). Pinned by `GraceOwnershipSemanticsTests` and the spec cases `grace-saturation-is-valid`, `grace-in-branch-nested-block-belongs-to-the-block` and `grace-on-branch-binder-in-nested-block-rejected`.
- **Rules:** PAR-06 (title, status, law, rule, examples, boundary, tension, evidence), PAT-04 (status, rule, boundary, tension, evidence), DOT-06 and SYN-12 (wording), the PAR and PAT topic tails. PAR-03, PAR-04, PAR-05, PAR-07, FORMAL-02/03 and RUN-04 are unchanged (checked: they already state the corollaries — Grace under a closed list is an error, own names before forwarded names, Grace is C#-only, deferred units are validated when selected).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q16-grace-investigation/final-report.md`; implementation `../q16-grace-implementation/` (`final-report.md`, `constitution.md`, `compatibility.md`).

#### Q-10 — Is `DisplayDecimals` language or host policy? (X-35; oq RUN-03) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-07 (D-F: composable source and host display filters); EXTENDED BY OWNER DECISION 2026-11-12 (two independent settings, `MinDecimalPlaces` and `MaxDecimalPlaces`; `DisplayDecimals` removed)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-07. Decision lineage: the investigation `../q28-q10-numeric-identity-display/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY) recommended D-O — no source display hook, host options only — with D-H (the engine convention as it stood) as the owner-override alternative. After a product-portability discussion the owner REJECTED D-O and adopted D-F, composable source and host display filters, which supersedes both D-H's simple source-over-host precedence and D-O. The question is closed; X-35 is resolved by decision as an intentional engine/evaluator boundary, and oq RUN-03 is closed with it.
- **Owner extension 2026-11-12 (D-F kept and extended to two settings; recorded here 2026-11-15 by the Constitution catch-up; C#-only host presentation policy with no Lean counterpart; implemented as `1d3e1354`, replacing the `DisplayDecimals` feature of issue #118):** the status stays RESOLVED BY DECISION (D-F). The owner replaced the one setting by TWO INDEPENDENT settings, `MinDecimalPlaces` (the fewest digits shown after the decimal point) and `MaxDecimalPlaces` (the most). Each is one integer in 0..99 (`RunOptions.DecimalPlacesLimit`, a validity bound, never a clamp), and each has the two origins D-F named: the program root's own property of that name, and the host (`RunOptions.MinDecimalPlaces` / `RunOptions.MaxDecimalPlaces`, the CLI's `--min-decimal-places` / `--max-decimal-places`).
  - *Composition per name.* Each setting composes only with its counterpart of the same name, by D-F's law: an absent one imposes nothing, one present one decides, both give their minimum, and neither origin overrides the other.
  - *Structural absence versus explicit zero.* Absence is a state of its own for each setting and each origin: a host `null` is no setting, and an explicit `0` is a real one.
  - *No cross-defaulting.* Neither setting supplies a value for the other: a minimum alone never rounds, a maximum alone never pads, and a fixed count is both at the same value.
  - *Read order in one run.* The output comes first. Only if it succeeded, the engine reads `MinDecimalPlaces` and then `MaxDecimalPlaces` by the ordinary cached zero-argument VALUE read in the same run, whatever the host settings are. A failing first read stops the run, and the second is not attempted.
  - *Source validation before composition.* Each source value is validated, the minimum first (one integral number in 0..99, else `IllegalInEval` at that property's declaration, never clamped); then the source pair is checked; then each setting is composed with the host's; then the effective pair is checked.
  - *Conflicts.* An effective minimum above the effective maximum is an error, never clamped, swapped or dropped. It is reported in four rows: inconsistent CLI options are a usage error at command-line parsing, before the source is read; an inconsistent `RunOptions` pair is a host `ArgumentException` where the run begins, never a source diagnostic; a source pair inconsistent with itself is `EvalFailure` / `IllegalInEval` whatever the host settings are; an effective pair inconsistent only across origins is `EvalFailure` / `IllegalInEval`. The two evaluation failures name both values and each one's origin (the program or the host; a value both origins supply equally is the program's) and are positioned at the program's `MinDecimalPlaces` declaration when the minimum is the program's, otherwise at `MaxDecimalPlaces`.
  - *Display rule.* With no setting from any origin the canonical display is unchanged (the stored digits). A non-finite value keeps its canonical spelling. Otherwise the value is rounded to the maximum when one is present (midpoints away from zero), written with the fewest fractional digits that represent it exactly (stored trailing zeros are removed), and padded with zeros to the minimum, with no decimal point when no fractional digit remains and with its sign kept, a zero's and a rounded-to-zero value's included. The text depends on the value, never on its stored quantum: `MinDecimalPlaces = 0` and `MaxDecimalPlaces = 99` are not "no setting", and integers are padded.
  - *Removal.* `DisplayDecimals`, `--display-decimals`, `RunOptions.DefaultDisplayDecimals`, `RunOptions.MaxDisplayDecimals` and `RunResult.WithHostDisplayDecimals` are gone without shims, deprecation or a migration diagnostic: a root `DisplayDecimals` is an ordinary property, and the option is an unknown one.
  - *Unchanged.* The X-35 boundary stands: raw `Evaluator.Run*` performs neither read and neither check.
  - *Witnesses (CLI built from `main`, 2026-11-15; `../constitution-catch-up-20261115/probe/probe.log`):* `MaxDecimalPlaces = 2` / `X = 1.555` / `X, X * 2 == 3.11` → `1.56`, `true`; `MinDecimalPlaces = 2` / `1.5, 10, 1.234567` → `1.50`, `10.00`, `1.234567`; `MaxDecimalPlaces = 4` / `10, 1.234567, 2.5000` → `10`, `1.2346`, `2.5`; both at 2 / `1.234567, 10, 2.5000` → `1.23`, `10.00`, `2.50`; `MaxDecimalPlaces = 7` / `1 / 3` with no host setting, a host maximum of 5 and one of 10 → 7, 5 and 7 places; `MinDecimalPlaces = 4` / `5` under a host maximum of 2 → `IllegalInEval`, "the minimum is 4 (from the program) and the maximum is 2 (from the host)"; `MinDecimalPlaces = 3` / `MaxDecimalPlaces = 1` / `5` → `IllegalInEval`, under a host minimum of 0 too; `MaxDecimalPlaces = tick()` / `MinDecimalPlaces = tick()` / `tick()` → `1.00` (the minimum is read before the maximum); `DisplayDecimals = 2` / `1.555` → `1.555`; `--display-decimals 2` → unknown option.
  - *Rules:* RUN-06 (restated), RES-06, RUN-01 (exception 3), OP-14, VAL-11, SYN-01, SYN-13, RUN-02, RAND-01, FORMAL-03.
  - *Evidence on `main`:* `AGENTS.md` § DECIMAL PLACES ARE TWO INDEPENDENT, COMPOSABLE PRESENTATION SETTINGS; `docs/design/language-rules/evaluator-and-hosting.md` § Decimal places: minimum and maximum, source and host; `src/KatLang/SEMANTIC-ALIGNMENT.md` (the dated record that cites #118); `Hosting/DecimalPlacesCompositionTests`, `DecimalPlacesFormattingTests`, `DecimalPlacesConsistencyTests` and `HostDecimalPlacesTests`; the C#-only spec cases `max-decimal-places-rounds-ties-away-from-zero`, `min-decimal-places-pads-and-never-rounds`, `equal-min-and-max-decimal-places-fix-the-places` and `decimal-places-show-the-value-not-the-stored-digits`. The bullets below describe D-F as decided on 2026-10-07 for the one former setting; where they name `DisplayDecimals` or an upper bound only, they are history.
- **The decision (RUN-06, RUN-01 exception 3, RES-06):** the program root's own `DisplayDecimals` property and a host-configured display-decimal value (`RunOptions.DefaultDisplayDecimals`, the CLI's `--display-decimals`, a future KatLangWeb setting) are independent presentation filters with one role — an upper bound on displayed decimal places — and different origins. An absent filter imposes no limit; one present filter is effective; when both are present the effective count is their minimum; when neither is present rendering is canonical. A host value of `null` ("off") is no host filter — never zero places, never canonicalization, never a suppressed source filter. Source `DisplayDecimals` remains an engine-level host presentation convention, not core evaluator semantics: `KatLangEngine` reads the root's own zero-parameter property after successful output using the ordinary cached VALUE access in the same run (cache, budget, random stream, host operations, cancellation token), WHATEVER the host filter is; raw `Evaluator.Run*` does not perform the read. That read is evaluation — it can trace, draw, spend steps, be cancelled and fail — so an invalid or failing source filter fails the engine run with its own error even under a stricter host filter; only the rendering step is inert, and it never changes a value, a representation, `.string`, or anything already evaluated. Only the root's own declaration is special. A shared program therefore carries its display intent: `DisplayDecimals = 7` shows 7 places without a host filter, 5 under a host filter of 5, and still 7 under 10.
- **Rejected alternatives:** D-H (simple source-over-host precedence: a looser source setting overrode a stricter host filter); D-O (host options only: loses source-carried display intent — the investigation's recommendation, rejected by the owner); D-L (a language-level hook read by every entry point, rejected by the investigation); D-S (a static literal-only directive, not adopted).
- **Canonical examples (three engine routes; the CLI alike):** source 7 / host absent → 7 places; source absent / host 5 → 5; source 7 / host 5 → 5; source 5 / host 7 → 5; source 0 / host 7 → 0; source 7 / host 0 → 0; source 99 / host 99 → 99; under host 5, `DisplayDecimals = 1 / 0` → `DivisionByZero` and `DisplayDecimals = 100` → `IllegalInEval`; `DisplayDecimals = trace(7)` traces exactly once under host off / 5 / 10 and shows 7 / 5 / 7 places; with source 2 and host 1, `x = 1.555` displays `1.6` while `x.string` is `'1.555'` and `x == 1.555` is `true`; the raw evaluator never traces or fails on a source filter.
- **Compatibility:** D-F differs from D-H only when both filters are present and the host filter is the smaller: the rendered text then uses the host's count. Values, Decimal128 representations, `.string`, errors, effects, draws, steps and route agreement are unchanged; invalid, failing and effectful source filters behave exactly as under D-H, beside a host filter too (`../q28-q10-nf-df-implementation/compatibility.md`).
- **Implementation (2026-10-07, working tree over `main` @ `83819f30`):** one production change — `KatLangEngine.CombineDisplayDecimals(source?, host?)`, the one minimum composition, called by `ResolveDisplayOptions`. The engine's post-output read (`RunCountedWithTopLevelProperty` and its async twin, `EvalTopLevelZeroArgPropertyCounted` and its twin) and every validation diagnostic are unchanged (the D-O plan to delete them is superseded). XML documentation (`RunOptions.DefaultDisplayDecimals` — its name kept for this release, documented as the host filter — `RunOptions.MaxDisplayDecimals`, `KatLangEngine`, `BoundedOutputWriter`, `ExactOutputFormatter`, `ValueTextRenderer`), the CLI help (`--display-decimals` is a display filter; the smaller count applies), README, tutorial, generator guidance and the language-rules documentation follow. No public signature change; Lean unchanged (it models no rendering). Pinned by `Hosting/DisplayDecimalsFilterCompositionTests`; the D-H precedence pins in `DefaultDisplayDecimalsTests`, `DisplayDecimalsHostileReviewTests`, `HostApiContractTests`, `HostilePublicApiTests`, `PublicFormatterExtensionTests`, the concurrency corpus and the CLI tests were repinned to the minimum law.
- **Rules:** RUN-06 (rule, status, boundary, tension), RUN-01 (exception 3), RES-06 (rule sentence, boundary), the RUN topic tail (display-setting mechanics; its open question closed), OP's non-constitutional display bullet, SYN-01's spelling inventory, PROP's non-constitutional bullet, COVERAGE row L02. RUN-02 and RAND-01 are unchanged: they already state that the read shares the run's state after the output.
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q28-q10-numeric-identity-display/final-report.md`, `q10.md` (recommending D-O); implementation `../q28-q10-nf-df-implementation/` (`q10.md`, `display-filter.md`, `decision-lineage.md`, `katlangweb-handoff.md`).

#### Q-28 — What "the same value" means on the Decimal128 tier (X-28, X-12; oq NUM-01, FAM-09) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-07 (N-F: equality is `==`; a repeated name keeps the first equally rich representative)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-07. The owner adopted N-F of `../q28-q10-numeric-identity-display/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY; the investigation recommended N-F). The question is closed; X-28 and X-12 are resolved, and oq NUM-01 and FAM-09 are closed with it.
- **The decision (VAL-11, PAT-09, PAT-05, NEED-04):** "the same value" is `==` — `Decimal128.Equals` at numeric leaves (NaN is one value, `-0 == 0`, the quantum is ignored), recursive structural equality over sequences and lists — for every consumer: `==`/`!=`, `contains`, the classes of `distinct`, numeric literal patterns, duplicate clause heads and repeated-name VALUE compatibility; there is no second, representation-sensitive numeric equality. A number's Decimal128 representation (quantum, zero sign, NaN sign) is data the value carries, never provenance; value-carrying operations preserve it, `.string` observes it (OP-14), and presentation never changes it. A repeated name keeps ONE richest compatible complete contribution (NEED-04: VALUE + CALLABLE outranks VALUE only, in either order) and, among equally rich ones, the FIRST in written traversal order (left to right, depth first); the retained value, representation included, is that contribution's own — never a synthesized, canonicalized or leaf-wise merged representative. Permuting all contributions of one repeated name preserves satisfiability. On success it preserves the bound VALUE up to `==`, callable identity and channel availability; among equally rich compatible contributions, the first in written traversal order supplies the retained representation. Failure reporting follows ordinary binding order (NEED-04, PAT-10, Q-27): when different incompatibilities coexist, permutation may change the error category, blamed contribution, payload, message or span, although every permutation still fails. Numeric literal patterns match by `==` (`F(0)` matches `-0` and `0.0`; `F(1.5)` matches `1.50` and `3 / 2`), and `==`-equal literals are one clause head. Collections keep their operation-specific rules: `distinct` keeps the first occurrence of each class; `contains` is membership by `==`; `order` is stable and keeps every input representative; `orderDesc` is its exact reverse (COLL-06's separate equal-item question is not decided here); `min`/`max` follow OP-13, signed-zero law included, with same-signed quantum ties unspecified.
- **Owner follow-up (2026-10-07):** hostile review found that the earlier N-F reconciliation overstated the permutation law by including exact error category. Owner clarified that N-F governs compatibility and representative selection; NEED-04 + PAT-10 govern failure reporting. Satisfiability is permutation-invariant; exact failure category is not guaranteed when several incompatibilities coexist. Q-28 remains RESOLVED BY DECISION — N-F; X-28 remains resolved. The earlier overclaim remains in the historical implementation/review evidence, superseded by this correction.
- **Rejected alternatives:** N-C (a canonical representative, binder-local or global), N-E (representation-exact compatibility) and N-O (observational equality for merges) — measured by the investigation to change 376 (N-C binder-local), 508 (N-C global), 627 (an N-E implementation) and 490 (N-O) of 1,290 probe outcomes, where N-F changes none.
- **Canonical examples (six routes):** `P(x, x) = x.string` / `P(1.5, 1.50), P(1.50, 1.5), P(0, -0), P(-0, 0)` → `S['1.5', '1.50', '0', '-0']`; with `A = 1.50`, `P(1.5, A)` and `P(A, 1.5)` → `'1.50'`; `F(1.5) = 'hit'` / `F(x) = 'miss'` / `F(1.50), F(3 / 2), F(1.6)` → `S['hit', 'hit', 'miss']`; `Z(0) = 'zero'` / `Z(x) = 'other'` / `Z(-0), Z(0.0)` → `S['zero', 'zero']`; `distinct((1.0, 1))` → `L[1.0]`; `order((1.0, 1))` → `L[1.0, 1]`.
- **Compatibility:** none — N-F is the existing C# and Lean behavior (`Evaluator.BindNeedPatterns`, Lean `bindNeedName`, which keeps the earlier contribution unless a later one is strictly richer). The investigation measured 1,290 probe variants on six routes with no representation-level route disagreement; the implementation adds tests, spec cases and documentation only.
- **Implementation (2026-10-07, working tree over `main` @ `83819f30`):** no production code change. Permanent tests `NumericRepresentativeSelectionTests` (22 representation pairs × four shapes × five origins, families, callbacks, collections and literal patterns, compared representation-exactly — NaN sign and positive quantum included — on six routes); the C#-only spec cases `repeated-name-keeps-first-equally-rich-representative` and `decimal-literal-patterns-match-by-value` (with `LeanExclusionReason`s, exact-ID-pinned; `lean/LanguageSpecCases.lean` and both generator prompt blocks regenerated for their counts); a `SEMANTIC-ALIGNMENT.md` classification entry; documentation in AGENTS.md, `evaluator-and-hosting.md`, `call-by-need.md`, `sequences-lists-and-calls.md` and the tutorial; a comment-only tightening of the Lean permutation law's header.
- **Rules:** VAL-09 (status, boundary, tension), VAL-11 (new), PAT-05 (rule, boundary, tension), PAT-09 (status, rule, tension), PAT-10 (boundary), CMP-05 (title, rule, tension), COLL-06 (rule), COLL-07 (boundary), OP-13 (boundary), OP-14 (tension), FORMAL-04 (boundary, tests), NEED-04 (wording).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q28-q10-numeric-identity-display/final-report.md`, `q28.md`; implementation `../q28-q10-nf-df-implementation/` (`q28.md`, `numeric-model.md`).

#### Q-19 — Open deduplication by spelling vs identity (X-20; oq NAME-02) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06 (D-I: open targets that resolve to one provider count once, by the callable-identity relation)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06. The owner adopted D-I of `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY) together with Q-29 A-U, Q-31 H-P and Q-32 I-U as one law system. The question is closed; X-20 is resolved, and oq NAME-02 is closed with it.
- **The decision (RES-03):** at one open level, written targets that resolve to the SAME provider — the same declaration in the same declaring scope and activation, NEED-04's one callable-identity relation — count once (the first occurrence names it); distinct providers count separately whatever their text. Spelling is no longer an identity: `open Sub, Lib.Sub` (one declaration) is one provider; `open M, M` and `open M, (M)` are unchanged; two textually identical inline blocks stay two providers; `open 'u', 'u'` and `open A, B` over two loads of one URL are one provider (Q-32). A member ALIAS is its own binding (FWD-02), so `open A, B` with `B.X` an alias of `A.X` stays two providers of `X`.
- **Rejected alternatives:** D-S (keep spelling-keyed deduplication and document it — one declaration reached through two spellings stays ambiguous); D-E (a front-end duplicate-target diagnostic — it rejects accepted source such as `open M, M`).
- **Canonical examples (six routes, Lean agreeing):** inside `Lib = { public Sub = { public X = 1 } ⏎ public R = { open Sub, Lib.Sub ⏎ X } }`, `Lib.R` → `1` in either order (formerly `AmbiguousOpen`); `open M, (M)` → `1`; `open { public X = 1 }, { public X = 1 }` with a written `X` → `AmbiguousOpen` (two declarations).
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-06, `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 314 probe cells (12 corpora) on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `4960e80` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: 191 cells are unchanged and 123 change — 42 successful programs change value, 22 run-time `AmbiguousOpen`s and 6 other run-time errors succeed, 16 successful programs become run-time errors, 13 successful programs and 19 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 4 run-time errors change their report (one `LocalOnlyProperty` becomes `ArityMismatch` — a module member that read the site's parameter now declares it — and three keep their code with new wording), and 1 front-end rejection (a holder-parameter `ParameterPropertyCollision`) becomes accepted. Every changed cell is the change the investigation predicted for the decided system (its `rec` prototype): 121 with the identical new outcome, 2 differing only in the A-U message wording; none unexpected, none missing. Route agreement is identical in both trees (277 of 314 cells agree on all six routes; the other 37 are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes), and Lean agrees with C# on every encoded module program (10/10, where the investigation's prototype without the rooted mark agreed on 7/10) and on the open corpora (14/14, 2/2, 4/4).
- **Implementation (2026-10-06, working tree over `main` @ `4960e80`):** the evaluators resolve each target and drop one whose identity equals an earlier one (C# `Evaluator.ResolveAllOpens` with `SameRepeatedCallableIdentity`, Lean `resolveAllOpens` with `sameRepeatedCallableIdentity`; an unidentified hand-built Lean declaration counts as its own provider); the front end computes the same identity statically once (`OpenProviderIdentity`: the provider's declaration and its declaring owners to the root level, a written block and a loaded module declared at the root level), read by elaborated lookup (`ElaboratedScopeLookup.ResolveOpenProvider` / `GetResolvedOpenProviders`, and with it detection, the static ambiguity check and the editor), exposure settlement (`OpenLevelSettlement`), the summary channel (`ResolvedOpenCandidate`, `DistinctProviders`) and the resolver (`OpenProvider.ResolveProvider`); `Evaluator.OpenTargetDedupKey` remains only a pre-resolution optimization.
- **Rules:** RES-03 (rule: providers by identity; boundary), RES-06 (tension), MOD-09 (rule: open providers).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md`, `q19-open-dedup.md`; implementation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/` (`q19.md`, `open-provider-identity.md`); `OpenProviderIdentityTests`, `CoreTests/OpenProviderIdentity.lean`, spec cases `open-two-spellings-one-provider`, `open-identical-inline-blocks-two-providers`, `open-distinct-declarations-stay-distinct-providers`.

#### Q-29 — An ambiguous open: a static diagnostic, or a run-time error only? (X-26; oq NAME-01) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06 (A-U: overlap is valid; a written ambiguous name is a front-end error at the use)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06. The owner adopted A-U of `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY). The question is closed; X-26 is resolved, and oq NAME-01 is closed with it.
- **The decision (RES-03, RES-04):** distinct providers (after Q-19's identity dedup) may publicly expose the same name; the overlap is valid source and nothing is reported for a name that is never written. A WRITTEN name whose resolution reaches an open level where two or more distinct providers publicly provide it denotes no declaration: it is the front-end error `AmbiguousOpen` at that occurrence, whether or not evaluation would ever demand it — in a closed list, an inferring body, an unselected branch, an uninvoked callback and a zero-iteration loop alike (validity is static: Model C keeps directly written undeclared names static, Q-15; NEED-05/MOD-10 "call-by-need is not declaration validity"). A statically certain (MUST-selected) dot-fallback name is a written name (Q-75); a dot edge whose member resolves structurally is no use of the opened name at all. A lookup the front end cannot decide — a MAY-selected dot fallback, a host-built tree — keeps the run-time `AmbiguousOpen`. A use inside a deferred unit is judged when the unit is selected (MOD-10), never before.
- **Public API:** one new `DiagnosticCode` member, `AmbiguousOpen` (value 52), mapped onto the existing same-named `KatLangErrorCode.AmbiguousOpen` (the `IllegalInOpen` precedent); no `KatLangErrorCode` member is added, removed or renumbered.
- **Rejected alternatives:** A-R (keep the run-time error only — an unread ambiguity stays accepted and a reference's meaning depends on demand); A-D (a declaration-time overlap diagnostic — adding an unused member to a library would break every program that opens it beside another).
- **Canonical examples (six routes):** `open A, B` (both `X`) / `Y = X` / `5` → front-end `AmbiguousOpen` at that `X` (formerly `ok 5`); `open A, B` / `5` → `5`; `open A, B` / `A.X + B.X` → the sum; with `K(p) = { open L1, L2 ⏎ p.X }`, `K(10)` → run-time `AmbiguousOpen` (receiver-decided fallback); `K = { open L1, L2 ⏎ 5.X }` → front-end `AmbiguousOpen` at the member token.
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-06, `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 314 probe cells (12 corpora) on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `4960e80` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: 191 cells are unchanged and 123 change — 42 successful programs change value, 22 run-time `AmbiguousOpen`s and 6 other run-time errors succeed, 16 successful programs become run-time errors, 13 successful programs and 19 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 4 run-time errors change their report (one `LocalOnlyProperty` becomes `ArityMismatch` — a module member that read the site's parameter now declares it — and three keep their code with new wording), and 1 front-end rejection (a holder-parameter `ParameterPropertyCollision`) becomes accepted. Every changed cell is the change the investigation predicted for the decided system (its `rec` prototype): 121 with the identical new outcome, 2 differing only in the A-U message wording; none unexpected, none missing. Route agreement is identical in both trees (277 of 314 cells agree on all six routes; the other 37 are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes), and Lean agrees with C# on every encoded module program (10/10, where the investigation's prototype without the rooted mark agreed on 7/10) and on the open corpora (14/14, 2/2, 4/4).
- **Implementation (2026-10-06, working tree over `main` @ `4960e80`):** one new public `DiagnosticCode.AmbiguousOpen` (value 52) mapped onto the existing `KatLangErrorCode.AmbiguousOpen`, reported by `ParameterDetector.ReportAmbiguousOpenUse` over `ElaboratedScopeLookup.FindAmbiguousOpenProviders` in the rewrite walk over the rows a body writes, at the occurrence; a dot edge's fallback name is a use only when `LexicalFallbackSelectionOf` is `Always` (member token); the message names the providers as written and the two repairs; Lean models no front-end rule (FORMAL-02).
- **Rules:** RES-03 (rule: where ambiguity is reported; tension), RES-04 (tension).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md`, `q29-ambiguity.md`; implementation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/` (`q29.md`, `static-ambiguity.md`); `StaticAmbiguousOpenTests`, spec cases `ambiguous-open-written-use-is-static`, `ambiguous-open-unused-overlap-is-valid`.

#### Q-31 — Module hygiene (X-37; oq MOD-01) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06 (H-P: a module is its own prelude-rooted source unit)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06. The owner adopted H-P of `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY). The question is closed; X-37's hygiene half is resolved, PV-42 is resolved by decision, and oq MOD-01 is closed with it.
- **The decision (MOD-06, MOD-08, RES-07):** a loaded module — property-held, opened, or nested in another module — is a separately rooted source unit: its free names resolve against its own declarations and then the prelude (builtins, `Math` and its aliases, the run's host operations) and nothing else; a name it cannot resolve becomes an implicit parameter of its own member that uses it (PAR-03, MOD-06). The load site's properties, parameters, opened names and prelude shadows never capture a module name; a site parameter reaches a module member only as an argument — explicit, bare forwarding or formula lifting by name (FWD-02, PAR-07, unchanged). So `open 'u'` ≡ `M = load('u')` + `open M` (PV-42's asymmetry is gone), and one module text has one meaning, one signature set and one validity everywhere.
- **Rejected alternative:** H-L (load-site capture as law — one URL would mean different things and have different signatures at different sites, a client's `sum` or `Base` would silently rewrite library code, and one URL could not be one binding).
- **Canonical examples (six routes, Lean agreeing on the elaborated trees):** `sum(xs) = 999` / `M = load(sum.kat)` / `M.V` → `3` (formerly `999`); `Base = 10` / `M = load(free.kat)` / `M.V` → `ArityMismatch` and `M.V(10)` → `11` (formerly `11` and `ArityMismatch`); `G(n) = { M = load(param.kat) ⏎ M.V }` / `G(5)` → `6` by bare forwarding of `n`; `F(a) = { M = load(pa.kat) ⏎ M.a }` is no longer a `ParameterPropertyCollision`. Deferred branches keep their schedule (MOD-10).
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-06, `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 314 probe cells (12 corpora) on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `4960e80` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: 191 cells are unchanged and 123 change — 42 successful programs change value, 22 run-time `AmbiguousOpen`s and 6 other run-time errors succeed, 16 successful programs become run-time errors, 13 successful programs and 19 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 4 run-time errors change their report (one `LocalOnlyProperty` becomes `ArityMismatch` — a module member that read the site's parameter now declares it — and three keep their code with new wording), and 1 front-end rejection (a holder-parameter `ParameterPropertyCollision`) becomes accepted. Every changed cell is the change the investigation predicted for the decided system (its `rec` prototype): 121 with the identical new outcome, 2 differing only in the A-U message wording; none unexpected, none missing. Route agreement is identical in both trees (277 of 314 cells agree on all six routes; the other 37 are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes), and Lean agrees with C# on every encoded module program (10/10, where the investigation's prototype without the rooted mark agreed on 7/10) and on the open corpora (14/14, 2/2, 4/4).
- **Implementation (2026-10-06, working tree over `main` @ `4960e80`):** every front-end pass processes a loaded-module root through a module arm, prelude-rooted and once per operation (`ParameterDetector.ProcessModuleRoot`, `ImplicitArgumentResolver.ProcessModuleRoot`, `PropertyExposureResolver.ProcessModuleRoot`, the collision and open-provider validators, the provenance finalizer; `ModuleUnits`), error-free operations publish their units to the document loader's `ModuleUnitRegistry` so a deferred materialization reaches the same declaration, `ElaboratedPropertyScope` roots a module level at the chain root, the summary channel settles a module at the prelude and the sibling channel reads nothing in it, provider identities and the static alias chase restart at a module; at run time `Evaluator.WithParent` wires a module root under the chain's root level (Lean `Algorithm.withParent` over the new `PropertyIdentity.module`, kept by `identifyPropertyAlgorithm` and emitted by `LeanAstEncoder` for every C# module root; `staticAliasStep?` restarts its chain at a module).
- **Rules:** MOD-06 (title and rule), MOD-07 (rule: splicing), MOD-08 (replaced), PAR-03 (boundary), PROP-08 (boundary), RES-07 (caveat).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md`, `q31-hygiene.md`; implementation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/` (`q31.md`, `module-hygiene.md`); `ModuleHygieneTests`, `CoreTests/ModuleUnits.lean`.

#### Q-32 — Module identity (X-37, X-03; oq MOD-02) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06 (I-U: one declaration per canonical URL per compiled program, as the consequence of H-P)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-06. The owner adopted I-U of `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY). The question is closed; X-37 is resolved, PV-41 is resolved by decision, X-03 is unchanged, and oq MOD-02 is closed with it.
- **The decision (MOD-09, PROP-07):** within one compiled program, one canonical module URL denotes ONE module declaration; every load and every `open 'u'` of that URL — in any scope, at any position, eager or in a selected deferred unit — denotes it. Fetch and template identity are the canonical URL (Q-71/MOD-09, unchanged); each member is ONE binding: one zero-parameter value per run (PROP-04/07; no load site, holder or scope takes part) and one callable identity (NEED-04). A property holding a module (`P = load(u)`) is its own binding: a bare read of `P` (the module's output) caches under `P`, as a callable alias's bare read does (FWD-02). Distinct canonical URLs with identical bytes stay distinct sources and declarations. Under load-site capture this identity would be impossible (one binding would need two values); it follows from H-P (Q-31) and, with Q-19's D-I, makes `open A, B` over two loads one provider.
- **Rejected alternatives:** I-S (one declaration per splice scope — HEAD's incidental behavior, with no scoping rationale for its sibling and open-list rules); I-D (one declaration per directive — canonical-equivalent spellings would split after one fetch, and a member's host effect would run once per directive).
- **Canonical examples (six routes, seed 7):** two loads in different bodies share one draw (`S[976796, 976796]`, formerly `S[976796, 475339]`); `X = { open 'u' ⏎ R }` and `Y = { open 'u' ⏎ R }` share it; `A = load(t)` / `B = load(t)` / `A.T, B.T, A.T()` → `S[1, 1, 2]` with two ticks; `P(f, f) = f` / `P(A.X, B.X)` over two loads → `5` (one callable); two URLs serving identical bytes → two draws, and `open A, B` over them is `AmbiguousOpen` for a written `X`.
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-06, `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 314 probe cells (12 corpora) on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `4960e80` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: 191 cells are unchanged and 123 change — 42 successful programs change value, 22 run-time `AmbiguousOpen`s and 6 other run-time errors succeed, 16 successful programs become run-time errors, 13 successful programs and 19 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 4 run-time errors change their report (one `LocalOnlyProperty` becomes `ArityMismatch` — a module member that read the site's parameter now declares it — and three keep their code with new wording), and 1 front-end rejection (a holder-parameter `ParameterPropertyCollision`) becomes accepted. Every changed cell is the change the investigation predicted for the decided system (its `rec` prototype): 121 with the identical new outcome, 2 differing only in the A-U message wording; none unexpected, none missing. Route agreement is identical in both trees (277 of 314 cells agree on all six routes; the other 37 are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes), and Lean agrees with C# on every encoded module program (10/10, where the investigation's prototype without the rooted mark agreed on 7/10) and on the open corpora (14/14, 2/2, 4/4).
- **Implementation (2026-10-06, working tree over `main` @ `4960e80`):** every front-end pass processes a loaded-module root through a module arm, prelude-rooted and once per operation (`ParameterDetector.ProcessModuleRoot`, `ImplicitArgumentResolver.ProcessModuleRoot`, `PropertyExposureResolver.ProcessModuleRoot`, the collision and open-provider validators, the provenance finalizer; `ModuleUnits`), error-free operations publish their units to the document loader's `ModuleUnitRegistry` so a deferred materialization reaches the same declaration, `ElaboratedPropertyScope` roots a module level at the chain root, the summary channel settles a module at the prelude and the sibling channel reads nothing in it, provider identities and the static alias chase restart at a module; at run time `Evaluator.WithParent` wires a module root under the chain's root level (Lean `Algorithm.withParent` over the new `PropertyIdentity.module`, kept by `identifyPropertyAlgorithm` and emitted by `LeanAstEncoder` for every C# module root; `staticAliasStep?` restarts its chain at a module).
- **Rules:** MOD-09 (replaced), MOD-07 (rule: the holder binding), MOD-10 (rule: at selection), PROP-07 (tension resolved), RAND-01 (example), RES-03 (rule: open providers).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-open-module-identity/final-report.md`, `q32-module-identity.md`; implementation `../q19-q29-q31-q32-implementation/` (`q32.md`, `module-identity.md`); `ModuleIdentityTests`, `CoreTests/ModuleUnits.lean`, `LeanAstEncoderTests.LoadedModuleRoot_*`.

#### Q-17 — `.string` against a declared member named `string` (X-21; oq DOT-01) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-05 (S-C: a declared member named `string` wins; on a structural miss the intrinsic takes the extension call's place)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-05. The owner adopted option S-C of `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY), the entry's option (c) "let the member win", in the form in which the intrinsic takes the extension call's place. The question is closed; X-21 is resolved, PV-22 is resolved by decision, and oq DOT-01 is closed with it.
- **The decision (the dot route; DOT-01, DOT-08):** an ordinary non-spread edge `R.n(args?)` resolves in ONE order, from one property lookup: (1) a DECLARED structural member `n` wins whatever its spelling — `string` included — and accessibility is checked after selection (`LocalOnlyProperty`); (2) a member declared only in clause branches is `LocalOnlyProperty`; (3) on a structural MISS, `n == string` is the number-to-text intrinsic, whose receiver demand, kinds, zero parameters, argument rejection and text are unchanged (DOT-08, OP-14); (4) otherwise the edge is the extension fallback `n(R, args)` (DOT-03). A lexical `string` is never consulted by `.string`, `R*.n(args)` stays the lexical call `n(R*, args)` (DOT-07), and declarations named `string` stay legal. Every view follows the route: receiver navigation (`Obj.string.Q`), the CALLABLE projection, the alias static path, the static structural-member classification, the formula-lifting edge kinds, the sibling-dependency walk and the editor (a declared `string` member resolves to its declaration, an intrinsic edge to the builtin).
- **Rejected alternatives:** S-A (keep the intrinsic first and document it — a declared member stays silently unreachable, the one spelling-selected dot arm against "identity decides, spelling never"); S-B (reserve `string` as a member name with a declaration diagnostic — it rejects valid programs that never use `.string` and needs a scope rule of its own).
- **Canonical examples (six routes, Lean agreeing):** `Obj = { public string = 5 ⏎ 7 }` / `Obj.string` → `5`; with `public string(x) = x * 2`, `Obj.string(5)` → `10` and `Apply(Obj.string, 5)` → `10`; a member block `public string = { public Q = 3 ⏎ 4 }` makes `Obj.string.Q` → `3`; a local-only or branch-only member named `string` is `LocalOnlyProperty`; with `string(x) = 99` and `Obj = { public V = 1 ⏎ 7 }`, `3.string, Obj.string, string(3)` → `'3', '7', 99`; `Use(o) = o.string` / `Use(12)` → `'12'`.
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-05, `../q17-q18-q75-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 1,062 probe cells on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `ad3d7dd` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: the baseline equals the investigation's head on all 1,062 cells; 682 cells are unchanged, 49 change diagnostic wording only, 38 successful programs change value, 44 successful programs become run-time errors, 50 successful programs and 34 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 87 run-time errors succeed and 78 run-time errors change category; no front-end rejection becomes accepted. Every changed cell is attributed by the investigation's single-question prototypes (S-C 156, C-B3 160, F-A 43, S-C with C-B3 20, S-C with F-A 1; none unattributed, none from the combination alone), and the candidate equals the investigation's recommended prototype on 962 of the 1,056 shared cells, the other 94 differing in message text only (the computed-callee and receiver-aware F-A wordings; codes, spans, categories, locations and effects identical). Route agreement 1,060/1,062 and budget agreement 1,062/1,062 in both trees (the two route cells are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes, identical before and after); Lean agrees with C# on all 902 Lean-representable cells of the candidate (913 checked; the other 11 are C#-only Math cells, as at the baseline). S-C alone changes 156 cells and, with C-B3, 20 more; every one declares or reaches a member named `string`, and no program without such a member changes. One accepted program becomes a front-end error by FWD-02: `K(z) = Obj.string` with `public string(x)` is now bare forwarding of that parameterized member (`UnforwardableParameter`).
- **Implementation (2026-10-05, working tree over `main` @ `ad3d7dd`):** Lean `evalDotCallCounted` decides the route from ONE `lookupPropDefAny?` (the intrinsic only in its `none` arm), and the `string` short-circuits are gone from `resolveDotReceiver`, `projectNeedStructuralMember`, `Expr.staticAliasPath?` and `evalDotStringReceiverValue`; C# `EvalDotCallCounted` and its async twin likewise, with `ResolveDotReceiver`, the callable projection, the alias paths (`StaticAliasTargets.IsStaticPath`, `ResolveAliasStep`), the static views (`AstHelpers.ResolveStaticStructuralMemberProvider`, `FormulaLiftingRoles.EdgeKind`, `ImplicitArgumentResolver.EdgeKindOf`, `PropertyDependencyGraph`) and the editor (`SemanticModelBuilder.ResolveDotMember`) treating a `string` edge as any edge; a declared `string` member without output reports its own missing output (`MissingOutput.IsSelectedMemberOutput`), never the receiver's.
- **Rules:** DOT-01 (rule: the route), DOT-02 (rule: a `.string` edge is navigated), DOT-08 (title, rule, caveats, status), RES-06 (the deliberate-exception sentence and its `.string` caveat).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md`, `q17-string.md`, `policy-options.md`; implementation `../q17-q18-q75-implementation/` (`q17.md`).

#### Q-18 — Dot expressions on the algorithm channel (X-20; oq DOT-02) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-05 (C-B3: one callable identity in every position; the supplied position was settled by Model C on 2026-10-03)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-05. The owner adopted option C-B3 of `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY) — the entry's option (b), in its strictest form — for the callee position that the 2026-10-03 partial resolution left open. The question is closed; PV-09 is resolved by decision, X-20 is narrowed to its Q-19 row, and oq DOT-02 is closed with it.
- **The decision (DOT-09, SYN-09):** *a dot expression has ONE callable identity in every algorithm-capable position* — supplied argument, forwarded parameter, builtin callback, loop step and callee. An argumentless dot path whose every edge selects a declared structural member (DOT-02, with its accessibility check) carries that member's own callable, aliases normalized and members of members kept; every other dot expression — a lexical-fallback edge, an intrinsic `.string` edge, an argument-bearing edge — is a calculation value with no callable identity, and calling it is `NotAnAlgorithm`. Parentheses never change identity: `(Box.G)(2)` ≡ `Box.G(2)` (one frame naming the member), and `(Box.V)()` is the fresh call `Box.V()`, which neither reads nor populates `Box.V`'s cache entry. In syntax, a call may follow only a name, a graced name, an argumentless dot edge, or a redundant group of one of these: `X.Mk(1)()`, `R.M(a)()` and `R.M(a){…}` are `UnseparatedSameLineItem`, exactly like `Mk(1)()`. The qualified Math reference is an ordinary structural member reference (the C#-only exception is retired), so a user `Math = { public Abs(x) = 100 }` gives `100` for `(Math.Abs)(3)`, `Math.Abs(3)` and `map([1], Math.Abs)` alike.
- **Rejected alternatives:** C-A (keep the callee-position wrapper and restrict SYN-06's "`(F)(x)` ≡ `F(x)`" to names — a second, route-dependent identity and an exception to the parentheses law); C-B1/C-B2 (the member identity in callee position while an argument-bearing dot result stays callable or becomes a run-time error — the call gate would still accept a call after a computed result).
- **Canonical examples (six routes, Lean agreeing):** `Box = { public G(x) = x * 10 }` / `Box.G(2), (Box.G)(2), Apply(Box.G, 2)` → `20, 20, 20`; `Box = { public V = tick() }` / `Box.V, Box.V(), (Box.V)(), Box.V(), Box.V` → `1, 2, 3, 4, 1` (cached, fresh, fresh, fresh, cached) and `(Box.V)(), Box.V, (Box.V)(), Box.V` → `1, 2, 3, 2`; `Inc(x) = x + 1` / `(5.Inc)()` → `NotAnAlgorithm` "`5.Inc` is a computed value, not a callable"; `(5.string)()` → `NotAnAlgorithm`; `X = { public Mk(k) = k + 1 }` / `X.Mk(1)()` → `UnseparatedSameLineItem`; `(Math.Abs)(-3)` → `3` through the ordinary member.
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-05, `../q17-q18-q75-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 1,062 probe cells on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `ad3d7dd` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: the baseline equals the investigation's head on all 1,062 cells; 682 cells are unchanged, 49 change diagnostic wording only, 38 successful programs change value, 44 successful programs become run-time errors, 50 successful programs and 34 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 87 run-time errors succeed and 78 run-time errors change category; no front-end rejection becomes accepted. Every changed cell is attributed by the investigation's single-question prototypes (S-C 156, C-B3 160, F-A 43, S-C with C-B3 20, S-C with F-A 1; none unattributed, none from the combination alone), and the candidate equals the investigation's recommended prototype on 962 of the 1,056 shared cells, the other 94 differing in message text only (the computed-callee and receiver-aware F-A wordings; codes, spans, categories, locations and effects identical). Route agreement 1,060/1,062 and budget agreement 1,062/1,062 in both trees (the two route cells are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes, identical before and after); Lean agrees with C# on all 902 Lean-representable cells of the candidate (913 checked; the other 11 are C#-only Math cells, as at the baseline). C-B3 alone changes 160 cells and, with S-C, 20 more: grouped structural callees now run (`(Box.G)(2)`), grouped zero-argument member calls are fresh (3 successful programs change their cache observations), calls on computed dot results are `NotAnAlgorithm` (`(5.Inc)()` formerly ran through the wrapper), and calls written after an argument-bearing edge no longer parse.
- **Implementation (2026-10-05, working tree over `main` @ `ad3d7dd`):** ONE CALLABLE projection of a dot expression, C# `Evaluator.ProjectDotPathCallable`, now read by supply cells, by the callee (`ResolveCallee`, sync and async) and by the sequence optimizer's recognition (`ResolveAlgorithm`); Lean `resolveCalleeAlg` routes the callee of `evalCallCountedExpr` through `projectNeedStructuralMember` and `resolveAliasTarget` (law `callee_projection_is_supplied_projection`, guards `CoreTests/DotIdentity.lean`); a computed dot callee is `NotAnAlgorithm("dot result")`, rendered "`5.Inc` is a computed value, not a callable"; the parser's call gate admits `Expr.DotCall { Args: null }` only; the C#-only qualified-Math resolution (`TryResolveQualifiedMathNativeReference`) and the dead `HasRegistryProvenStrictValueFallback` / `IsStrictValueMathMember` are deleted, and `ResolveDotCallAlgorithm` / Lean `resolveAlg .dotMember` remain only as the receiver carrier of a dot result.
- **Rules:** DOT-03 (caveat), DOT-09 (title, rule, examples, caveats, tensions, status), ALG-02 (rule: the naming forms), ALG-05 (rule: a second argument list after a dot call), ALG-07 (rule: runtime wrappers), SYN-06 (caveat, tension), SYN-09 (rule: the call targets; caveats, tension), HO-01 (caveat), PROP-06 (tension, status), PROP-07 (tension, status), RES-07 and RES-09 (caveats), OP-11 (caveat); LOOP-08 and NEED-06 unchanged (a dated NEED-06 clarification in `docs/design/language-rules/call-by-need.md`, no new NEED law).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md`, `q18-callee.md`; implementation `../q17-q18-q75-implementation/` (`q18.md`).

##### Historical Q-18 record (2026-09-27 through 2026-10-05; superseded)

Kept verbatim from § Decide before release, where the entry stood until 2026-10-05 (its heading then read: "Dot expressions on the algorithm channel (X-20; oq DOT-02) — PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-10-03 (supplied position settled by Model C, NEED-06; callee position open)"). Its open assertions describe those dated snapshots; the resolution above is current.

- **PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-10-03 (pre-release re-baseline, `3f652da`).**
  - *Resolved by later law — the supplied position.* Model C's CALLABLE projection (NEED-06; Lean `projectNeedCallable` → `projectNeedStructuralMember`; the canonical spec case `repeated-dot-results-have-distinct-wrapper-identities`, now `5`; the result-value boundary) gives a supplied argumentless structural dot path its member's OWN callable and every other supplied dot expression none. Re-run on six routes, Lean agreeing: `Apply(Lib.F, 5)` is `10` like the opened `Apply(F, 5)`; `map([1, 2], Lib.Inc)`, `repeat(Lib.Step, 3, 0)` and `Lib.Step.repeat(2, 0)` work; `P(Lib.X, Lib.X)` and the mixed `P(Lib.X, X)` (opened) are `7` (one identity); `Call0(Box.V)` is a fresh call like `Call0(V)`; `F(p) = p.Q` / `F(Lib.Sub)` keeps Sub's members; `Twice(10.Sub(1))` and `Apply(5.Inc, 1)` are `NotAnAlgorithm` like `Twice(Sub(10, 1))`. Two of the three consequences this entry listed are gone (an argument-bearing dot result is no longer callable; `Lib.F` is `F` on the higher-order channel). DOT-09 and LOOP-08 now state it.
  - *Remaining (NEEDS DECISION) — callee position only.* A call written on a grouped dot expression, or after an argument-bearing edge, still resolves DOT-09's fresh memberless zero-parameter wrapper: `(Box.G)(2)` is `ArityMismatch` while `Box.G(2)` is `3`; `Box.V, (Box.V)(), Box.V()` is `1, 1, 2` (the grouped call reads the cache) while under `open Box` `(V)()` is a fresh call; `(Lib.F)(4)` fails while `(Math.Abs)(-3)` is `3` (the C#-only Math exception). Remaining options: (a) keep the wrapper in callee position and restrict SYN-06's "`(F)(x)` ≡ `F(x)`" to names; (b) give a grouped argumentless structural path its member's callable in callee position too, as NEED-06 does for supplied arguments (a Lean `resolveAlg` and C# change). Option (b) changes the outcome of accepted programs (`(Box.V)()`). Evidence: `../pre-release-question-rebaseline/question-dossiers.md` § Q-18.
- **Re-baseline 2026-10-01 (`d6b88a9`): NEEDS DECISION, unchanged.** `Twice(10.Sub(1))` `18` vs `Twice(Sub(10, 1))` `NotAnAlgorithm`; `Box.V, Box.V(), (Box.V)(), Box.V` `S[1, 2, 1, 1]`; `(Box.G)(2)` `ArityMismatch` vs `Box.G(2)` `3`; `P(Lib.X, Lib.X)` `TypeMismatch`; `Apply(Lib.F, 5)` `ArityMismatch` vs opened `10`; seeded `S[796, 339, 796, 796]` vs opened `S[796, 339, 489, 750]`. Evidence: `post-lifting-rebaseline/probes/dot/`.
- **Decision:** is the fresh memberless wrapper long-term law? Its consequences:
  - an argument-bearing dot result is callable while the equivalent call is not;
  - `Lib.F` is not `F`;
  - grouping changes freshness.
- **Options:**
  - (a) Document "`R.F(args) ≡ F(R, args)` on the value channel only", pin the user-module side, and restrict SYN-06's "`(F)(1)` is `F(1)`" to names.
  - (b) Give dotted paths member identity. This means narrowing the parser call gate (`Parser.cs:4351`) and changing Lean `resolveAlg .dotMember` and C# `ResolveDotCallAlgorithm` together.
- **Rules:** DOT-03, DOT-09, HO-01, ALG-05, ALG-07, PROP-06, PROP-07, SYN-06, SYN-09, LOOP-08.

#### Q-75 — Must a closed parameter list or a branch pattern require a statically MUST-selected dot-fallback name? (PV-15; post-lifting re-baseline, 2026-10-01) — RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-05 (F-A: a statically certain fallback name is a checked name)

- **Status:** RESOLVED BY DECISION 2026-10-05. The owner adopted option F-A of `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md` (verdict DECISION READY) — the entry's option (a) for every statically certain fallback, not only for definitely-absent receivers. The question is closed; PV-15 is resolved by decision.
- **The decision (DOT-05, PAR-04, DOT-03):** the existing `LexicalFallbackSelection` lattice decides, over the edge's structural-miss verdict (a `.string` edge has no fallback name): an INFERRING body collects the fallback name when the selection is not `Never` (unchanged); a CLOSED explicit parameter list or a clause-branch body checks it only when the selection is `Always` — a value receiver, or a statically known receiver that declares neither the member nor a branch-only member — and reports an unbound one as `UndeclaredIdentifier` at the member token, worded with the G-24 receiver clause and the known receiver's member suggestion, whether or not the definition is called. A MAY-selected fallback (`Conditional`: a parameter, an unresolved or ambiguous receiver, a navigated path over one) carries no static requirement — the runtime receiver may supply the member. Run-time behavior is unchanged.
- **Rejected alternative:** F-B (keep the declared-name check blind to dot edges and document that a closed list checks only names written as callees or values) — the dotted and plain spellings of one call would keep different static validity.
- **Canonical examples:** `Get(obj) = 5.size` / `7` → `UndeclaredIdentifier` at `size`, like `Get(obj) = size(5)`; `Get(obj) = obj.size` / `Get(Obj), Get(3)` with `Obj = { public size = 11 }` and `size(v) = 77` → `11, 77`; `F(0) = 0` / `F(n) = (n + 1).G` → `UndeclaredIdentifier` at `G`, uncalled or not; `F(x) = Math.Ceiling(x)` → `UndeclaredIdentifier` at `Ceiling`, "Did you mean 'Math.Ceil'?"; `Use(o) = o.string.Q` stays accepted (MAY).
- **Compatibility:** The production check (2026-10-05, `../q17-q18-q75-implementation/compatibility.md`) re-ran the investigation's 1,062 probe cells on six routes with its runner, built at the true baseline `ad3d7dd` (`git archive`) and against the candidate: the baseline equals the investigation's head on all 1,062 cells; 682 cells are unchanged, 49 change diagnostic wording only, 38 successful programs change value, 44 successful programs become run-time errors, 50 successful programs and 34 run-time errors become front-end rejections, 87 run-time errors succeed and 78 run-time errors change category; no front-end rejection becomes accepted. Every changed cell is attributed by the investigation's single-question prototypes (S-C 156, C-B3 160, F-A 43, S-C with C-B3 20, S-C with F-A 1; none unattributed, none from the combination alone), and the candidate equals the investigation's recommended prototype on 962 of the 1,056 shared cells, the other 94 differing in message text only (the computed-callee and receiver-aware F-A wordings; codes, spans, categories, locations and effects identical). Route agreement 1,060/1,062 and budget agreement 1,062/1,062 in both trees (the two route cells are the established deferred-region refusal of the synchronous generic and optimized routes, identical before and after); Lean agrees with C# on all 902 Lean-representable cells of the candidate (913 checked; the other 11 are C#-only Math cells, as at the baseline). F-A alone changes 43 cells and, with S-C, 1 more (`p.string.Q` is MAY under S-C, so the rejection the F-A prototype added there is gone); every change is a front-end rejection of a certain fallback name under a closed list or in a branch body, or of one inside a deferred branch when the branch is selected (MOD-10).
- **Implementation (2026-10-05, working tree over `main` @ `ad3d7dd`):** the DotCall arm of `ParameterDetector.CollectFreeParamsCore` collects a fallback name for an inferring body when the selection is not `Never` (unchanged) and checks it under a closed list or branch body when it is `Always`, over the structural-MISS verdict the detector stamps on every edge (`Expr.DotCall.ElaboratedMissSelection`, formerly `ElaboratedFallbackSelection`; `AstHelpers.GetStructuralMissSelection` / `LexicalFallbackSelectionOf`, which gives a `.string` edge `Never`); the report is `UndeclaredIdentifier` at the member token (`FindFirstResolveSpans` visits a checked edge's member between its receiver and its arguments) with the G-24 receiver clause and the known receiver's member suggestion; plain undeclared-name messages are unchanged.
- **Rules:** DOT-03 (static validity), DOT-04 (caveat), DOT-05 (rule, status), PAR-04 (rule, status).
- **Evidence:** investigation `../q17-q18-q75-dot-semantics/final-report.md`, `q75-static-fallback.md`; implementation `../q17-q18-q75-implementation/` (`q75.md`).

Q-15's Model-C resolution (a closed head's blocked lift is a runtime demand; "directly undeclared closed-list names … remain static errors") frames but does not decide it: whether a MUST-selected fallback member is a directly written name is exactly this choice, and AGENTS' uniform dotted-call equivalence and the G-24 pin ("receiver knowledge never changes validity") still pull in opposite directions.
- **Status:** OPEN — NEEDS DECISION. Opened by the post-lifting re-baseline so that PV-15's unresolved part has exactly one owner (PV-15 had none). No X or oq source.
